# Nimtto: the full text

> Every public page of nimtto.com (Nepal) and nimtto.com/international/ (worldwide), in plain text for AI engines. Updated 2026-10-18.

## Key facts
- Website: https://nimtto.com (Nepal, prices in rupees) and https://nimtto.com/international/ (worldwide, prices in US dollars)
- What it is: an animated invitation that opens like a real card, with an event website (schedule, maps, travel notes, story, photos, music) and RSVP, shared as one link. A real designer sets it up with the customer; guests need no app or account.
- Based in: Nepal. Works online with families in Nepal and couples and hosts worldwide.
- Contact: email nimttoz@gmail.com, WhatsApp +977 980-6393298 (English and Nepali). Replies usually within one business day.
- Payment: one payment, no subscription, no charge per guest. Nepal: Khalti, eSewa or bank QR (Fonepay), confirmed by hand. Abroad: card or PayPal in US dollars; the plan switches on as soon as the payment goes through.
- Delivery: the invitation appears in the customer's dashboard as soon as payment is confirmed; design help usually takes 1 to 3 business days. Invitations stay online for at least one year after the event date.
- Custom designs: an enquiry. Nimtto replies within one business day with a price.
- Refunds: payments are final; in a critical case a customer can ask, and Nimtto may approve a full or partial refund; problems with an invitation are fixed free. Terms: https://nimtto.com/terms/ · Privacy: https://nimtto.com/privacy/ · Refunds: https://nimtto.com/refunds/

## Prices
Nepal (https://nimtto.com/pricing/): Standard Rs 2,999; Pro Rs 4,999; Pro Max Rs 6,999; Custom from Rs 11,111.
International (https://nimtto.com/international/pricing/): Standard $49; Pro $99; Pro Max $149; Custom from $199.
Plans: Standard: A ready-made design, Your names, date and venue, Guest replies (RSVP), A link to share on WhatsApp. Pro: Everything in Standard, Photos and your story, Every ceremony with maps, Music and the opening scene. Pro Max: Everything in Pro, Premium designs, Personal guest links, Priority help until the wedding.

## Designs
Nepal site (27 wedding designs; the lowest plan that includes each):
- Standard: Kham (खाम): A paper envelope with a red wax seal. It opens into a clear card with all your events.; Mala (माला): A wedding mandap with red silk, marigold strings and brass kalash full of flowers.; Phoolbari (फूलबारी): A gate of fresh roses and marigold strings opens to show शुभ विवाह. Then a calm, soft invitation.; Dhaka (ढाका): Break the seal and slide off the Dhaka band. Your names rise out of the envelope among flowers.; Sayapatri (सयपत्री): A doorway hung with marigold strings. The strings lift to open a calm ivory invitation.; Chitra (चित्र): A picture book in Mithila art: the janti, the garlands, the seven rounds and the dance.; Jhyal (झ्याल): A carved Newari window. The wooden shutters open on शुभ विवाह.
- Pro: Dhoka (ढोका): A clean white card. The golden door of Patan opens in 3D to show your names.; Durbar (दरबार): A 3D morning walk through Bhaktapur Durbar Square, under flower arches.; Himal (हिमाल): Sunrise over the Himalaya, then a quiet photo story of the two of you.; Mandap (मण्डप): A 3D mandap on a bright morning. The couple exchange garlands and walk the seven rounds.; Bagaicha (बगैंचा): A 3D garden wedding: through a rose arch, around the sacred fire, on to the reception.; Ghar (घर): A warm evening walk through a Newar house, room by room, like a film.; Mangal (मंगल): A red temple door with garlands and bells. The doors swing open on शुभ विवाह.; Nimantrana (निमन्त्रणा): A traditional red and gold card that unfolds in 3D: Ganesh, the couple, then the programme.
- Pro Max: Mahal (महल): A golden palace gate tied with a satin bow. It opens onto a palace balcony at night.; Laali (लाली): Blush pink and gold. Lanterns drop in as an arched card draws itself.; Mehendi (मेहन्दी): Henna on ivory. A henna pattern draws itself, then two hennaed hands come together.; Hariyo (हरियो): A soft green garden in watercolour. The leaves part to show a white pavilion and two peacocks.; Shree (श्री): Deep plum and gold. A gold lotus opens on Ganesh as two diyas come down.; Pardaa (पर्दा): Red velvet curtains open on a mandap with a living fire. Each event has its own colours.; Rajdwar (राजद्वार): A painted gold palace gate with a satin bow. Untie it and walk through to a red and gold card.; Agni (अग्नि): The sacred fire at night. Tap to light it, then the couple walk the seven rounds.; Janti (जन्ती): Walk with the Naumati Baja band and the doli down an old Newari street to the bride’s door.; Swayambar (स्वयम्बर): Two fresh garlands swing apart. The bride’s side and the groom’s side come together as you scroll.; Sindoor (सिन्दूर): Red, white and black. The sindoor box opens and a red line carries your story.; Rangoli (रंगोली): A flower rangoli on a brick courtyard. The rings come together and the diyo in the middle lights up.

## Digital Wedding Invitation in Nepal With RSVP | Nimtto
URL: https://nimtto.com/
Animated wedding invitation website with RSVP, maps and Nepali dates, made with a real designer. Pay once from Rs 2,999 by eSewa, Khalti or bank QR.

### What is Nimtto?
Nimtto is an online invitation maker from Nepal. We make invitation websites for weddings, bratabandha, pasni, gunyu cholo and other family occasions. Your guests open one link on their phone and see every event, the date in Nepali and English, a map, your photos and a reply form.

### How much does a digital wedding card cost in Nepal?
A Nimtto invitation website costs Rs 2,999 (Standard), Rs 4,999 (Pro) or Rs 6,999 (Pro Max). A custom design made only for you starts at Rs 11,111. From abroad you can pay in US dollars by PayPal, from USD 49.

### Can guests reply to the invitation?
Yes. Guests tell you if they are coming, to which events and how many people. You read every reply in your own dashboard and can download the list.

### Can I send it on WhatsApp and Viber?
Yes. Your invitation is one link: share it on WhatsApp, Viber, Messenger or SMS. The preview shows your names and a picture. Guests open it in their phone browser, with no app, and everyone sees the same up-to-date details.

### Is an e-invitation acceptable in Nepal?
Yes. More Nepali families now send their invitation on WhatsApp or Viber, often with a few printed cards for elders. Guests like having the date, the venue and a map on their phone, and relatives abroad can open it anywhere.

### How long does it take?
We start as soon as your payment is confirmed and we have your details. A ready-made design is quicker than a custom one. Tell us your date when you order and we plan around it.

### Can I pay with eSewa or Khalti?
Yes. On the payment page, scan the QR with Khalti, eSewa or any bank app (Fonepay), with your order number in the remark. Then upload the payment screenshot and we confirm it, usually the same day. From abroad, pay by card or PayPal in US dollars.

### Do you make invitations for bratabandha, pasni and other occasions?
Yes. Besides weddings, we make invitation websites for engagement, bratabandha, gunyu cholo, pasni, nwaran, birthdays, janku, bhoj and receptions, and any family occasion. These are designed for you on the Custom plan.

### Do you serve outside Kathmandu?
Yes. Nimtto works online across Nepal: Kathmandu, Lalitpur, Bhaktapur, Pokhara, Butwal, Chitwan, Dharan, Biratnagar, Birgunj and everywhere else. We make your invitation with you on WhatsApp, and you pay by QR, so it does not matter where you live.

### When should I send the wedding card?
We suggest sending the online card three to four weeks before the wedding to guests in Nepal, and six to eight weeks before to relatives abroad, who need time to travel. Order your design a few weeks before that, so there is time for changes.

## Nepali Wedding Card Designs and Animated Invites | Nimtto
URL: https://nimtto.com/designs/
Browse 27 premium Nepali wedding card designs with animation, music and RSVP. Pick one and our designer personalises it for you. From Rs 2,999, paid once.

### What is the difference between Standard, Pro and Pro Max?
The plans differ in which designs and extras they include. Standard has 7 designs and all the basics. Pro adds 8 more designs, photos, every ceremony with maps and music. Pro Max includes every design, personal guest links and priority help.

### Can the invitation be in Nepali?
Yes. Every invitation works in English and Nepali, and guests switch with one tap. Dates show in Bikram Sambat and AD side by side.

### Can the date be in Bikram Sambat?
Yes. Every invitation shows the date in Bikram Sambat beside the AD date, with the day of the week, so elders and friends abroad read the same day. If your family uses the tithi or Nepal Sambat, tell us and we add it.

### Do guests need to install an app?
No. The invitation is a website. It opens in any phone browser from WhatsApp, Viber, Messenger or SMS, also on slow mobile data.

### Can I change details after the invitation is shared?
Yes. The link stays the same and changes show at once. You can update times, venues and photos from your dashboard, or message us and we change it for you.

### What is a custom design?
A custom design is a new invitation made only for you, with your colours, art and wording. It suits any occasion, not only weddings. It starts at Rs 11,111: tell us your idea in the order form and we reply within one business day with a price.

### Can I also print cards?
Yes. Many families send the online card to everyone and take a few printed cards to close elders by hand. Nimtto makes the online invitation; a local press can print matching cards if you show them your design.

## How to Make a Digital Wedding Invitation in Nepal | Nimtto
URL: https://nimtto.com/how-it-works/
Choose a design, pay once by eSewa, Khalti or bank QR, review it with your designer on WhatsApp, then send one link to every guest. Ready in days.

### How do I make an online wedding invitation in Nepal?
Choose a design on Nimtto, fill the short order form and pay by QR. We then message you on WhatsApp for your names, dates, photos and song, and send you the finished link to share.

### How long does it take?
We start as soon as your payment is confirmed and we have your details. A ready-made design is quicker than a custom one. Tell us your date when you order and we plan around it.

### When should I send the wedding card?
We suggest sending the online card three to four weeks before the wedding to guests in Nepal, and six to eight weeks before to relatives abroad, who need time to travel. Order your design a few weeks before that, so there is time for changes.

### How do I pay?
From abroad, you pay by card or PayPal on the payment page, and your plan switches on at once. In Nepal, you pay by Khalti, eSewa or any bank app by scanning the QR with your order number, then upload a screenshot and we confirm it.

### Why do I make an account when I order?
Your account lets you come back to your order, pay later, and later edit your invitation and read guest replies. You sign in with your email and the password you choose.

### Can I change details after the invitation is shared?
Yes. The link stays the same and changes show at once. You can update times, venues and photos from your dashboard, or message us and we change it for you.

### Can I send it on WhatsApp and Viber?
Yes. Your invitation is one link: share it on WhatsApp, Viber, Messenger or SMS. The preview shows your names and a picture. Guests open it in their phone browser, with no app, and everyone sees the same up-to-date details.

### What should I write on a Nepali wedding card?
Most cards open with a blessing, name the couple and both sets of parents, give the date in Bikram Sambat with the day and the AD date, the sait of the main rite, each ceremony with its time and venue, and the preetibhoj. They close with the hosts after निमन्त्रक or विनीत. Our wedding card page has samples in Nepali and English.

Your invitation stays online for at least one year after the event date, so guests can look back at the details and photos. If you would like it online for longer, ask us.

### What is a digital invitation website?
A digital invitation website is an invitation guests open on their phone, with a page of every detail behind it. With Nimtto it opens like a real card, then shows the schedule, maps, travel notes, your story and an RSVP form, all in one link you send by text or email.

### How much does a digital wedding invitation cost?
A Nimtto digital invitation costs $49 (Standard), $99 (Pro) or $149 (Pro Max), paid once. A design made just for your occasion starts at $199. There are no monthly fees and no charge per guest, so you can send it to as many people as you like.

### Is it a subscription?

URL: https://nimtto.com/wedding-invitation-nepal/

Wedding invitation cards online, made for Nepali weddings.. A Nimtto wedding card is an invitation website: it opens like a real card, then shows every ceremony from mehendi to reception with the date in Bikram Sambat and AD, a map, your photos and an RSVP. You share it as one link on WhatsApp or Viber, from Rs 2,999.

What your wedding card holds:
- An opening to remember: A door, a wax seal, a flower gate or a curtain opens before your names appear.
- Every ceremony: Mehendi, haldi, janti, the wedding and the reception, each with its own time, venue and map.
- Guest replies (RSVP): Who is coming, to which ceremony and how many. You read every reply and can download the list.
- Your song and photos: Your chosen song plays as it opens, with a gallery and a few lines about the two of you.

### What is a wedding invitation card online?
An online wedding card, or digital बिहेको निम्तो, is a wedding invitation your guests open on their phone from a WhatsApp or Viber message. With Nimtto it is a small website: it opens like a real card, then shows every ceremony, a map and a reply form.
Guests tap the link, watch a short opening, like a temple door, a wax seal or a gate of flowers, and see your names. Below that sit the programme from maagni to preetibhoj, each with a time, a venue and Google Maps, your photos, your song and a reply form. It works in English and Nepali, with the Bikram Sambat date beside the AD date.
You do not make it alone. You choose a design, pay once, and a Nimtto designer sets it up with you on WhatsApp, in English or Nepali. You see every change before anyone else does, and you can change times or venues even after you send it.

### The ceremonies on a Nepali wedding card
A Nepali wedding is a run of ceremonies over several days, and families name and order them differently. Bahun-Chhetri, Newar, Kirat, Madhesi, Tharu and other families each keep their own rites, and the order on the day depends on your priest. Mehendi and haldi are newer to Nepali weddings but now common, as Republica has reported. Use this list as a starting point; we list your events in your family’s order.
Wedding events often found on a Nepali card
Event | In Nepali | What guests need on the card
Engagement | माग्नी, टीका, औंठी | Date, place and who is invited
Mehendi | मेहेन्दी | Time and venue; usually close family and friends
Haldi | हल्दी | Time; many say what colour to wear
Janti departure | जन्ती प्रस्थान | Where to gather and the exact time (on the groom’s card)
Wedding ceremony | शुभ विवाह | The auspicious time (साइत), the venue and a map
Kanyadan | कन्यादान | Listed on the bride’s family card
Welcoming the bride | बधु भित्र्याउने | Listed on the groom’s family card
Reception or feast | प्रीतिभोज | Date, time, venue; often the largest guest list

### What to write on a Nepali wedding card
Traditional Nepali cards are sent by the family, not by the couple, and each family usually sends its own. The bride’s card lists the kanyadan; the groom’s card lists the janti departure and the bride’s welcome. These are the parts most cards include.
- An opening blessing, often ॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥, or one from your own tradition
- The couple’s names with the honorifics your family uses, such as चि. for the groom and सौ. for the bride
- The parents’ names and, often, the grandparents’
- The date in Bikram Sambat, with the day of the week, and the AD date for guests abroad
- The auspicious time (शुभ साइत) of the main rite
- Each ceremony with its time and venue
- The preetibhoj on its own line, as it often falls on another day or at another place
- The hosts after निमन्त्रक or विनीत, and a contact number
- A reply line, so you know numbers for the bhoj

### Nepali wedding card wording (बिहेको निम्तो नमुना)
Copy a sample, then change the names, dates and places. Your elders or family priest may prefer their own phrasing, and we set whatever words you send.
Bride’s family, formal:
॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥
हाम्री सुपुत्री सौ. प्रिया
र चि. आरवको शुभ विवाहको पावन अवसरमा
तपाईं सपरिवार उपस्थित भइदिनु हुन
हार्दिक निमन्त्रणा गर्दछौं।

मिति: शनिबार, ८ फागुन २०८३
कन्यादान: बिहान ११ बजे

निमन्त्रक
थापा परिवार
Groom’s family:
हाम्रा सुपुत्र चि. आरवको शुभ विवाहमा
तपाईंको शुभ उपस्थितिको अपेक्षा गर्दछौं।

जन्ती प्रस्थान: बिहान ८ बजे
बधु भित्र्याउने: बेलुका ५ बजे

विनीत
शर्मा परिवार
Preetibhoj:
प्रीतिभोज
मिति: आइतबार, ९ फागुन २०८३
समय: बेलुका ६ बजेदेखि
स्थान: होटल अन्नपूर्ण, काठमाडौं
English:
With the blessings of our elders,
the Thapa and Sharma families invite you
to the wedding of Priya and Aarav.
Saturday, 20 February 2027 (8 Falgun 2083)
Kanyadan at 11:00 AM
Reception on Sunday, 21 February, from 6:00 PM
Short, for WhatsApp:
Namaste! With great joy we invite you and your family to Priya and Aarav’s wedding on 8 Falgun 2083 (20 Feb 2027). All the details, the map and the reply form are here: [your link]
The dates are real calendar dates, given as examples only. Ask your priest for the lagan and the sait of your own wedding.

### When to send wedding cards in Nepal
There is no fixed rule in Nepal, and families in villages and cities do it differently. Wedding dates follow the lagan in the panchang, so many weddings fall in the same few months and venues, cooks and printers get busy. This is the timing we suggest for an online card.
A suggested timing for a Nepali wedding card
When | What to do
As soon as the lagan is fixed | Book the venue, then tell relatives abroad the date so they can plan travel
6 to 8 weeks before | Choose your design and order, so there is time for changes
4 to 6 weeks before | Send the link to relatives abroad and guests outside the valley
3 to 4 weeks before | Send the link to everyone; take printed cards to close elders if you have them
1 week before | Check replies and give the caterer your numbers for the bhoj
The day before | Update anything that moved; everyone with the link sees it

### Digital or printed wedding card in Nepal?
Printed cards are still loved in Nepal, especially on lokta paper, and many families still prefer a traditional card for close elders, as the Kathmandu Post has noted. At the same time, more and more invitations now arrive on WhatsApp and Viber. The choice most families make is both: an online card for everyone, and a few printed cards taken by hand to the elders who matter most.
Online and printed wedding cards in Nepal compared
 | Nimtto online card | Printed card
Cost | One payment, from Rs 2,999, for any number of guests | Priced per card, plus delivery
Reaching guests | Instant on WhatsApp, Viber or Messenger, in Nepal and abroad | By hand or by post; slow for relatives abroad
Changes | Change any time; everyone sees it | A reprint
Maps and programme | Every ceremony with time, venue and Google Maps | The programme only, as space allows
Replies | Built in, with numbers for the bhoj | Phone calls
For elders | Nepali with one tap; a family member can help | Familiar, and a card to keep. Paper wins here.

#### Is a digital wedding card acceptable in Nepal?
Yes. More Nepali families now send a digital wedding card on WhatsApp or Viber, often next to a few printed cards for elders. Guests like having the date, the venue and a map on their phone, and relatives abroad can open it anywhere. It saves printing and delivery, and you can change details at any time.

#### What goes in a Nepali wedding invitation?
A Nepali wedding invitation names the bride and groom and their parents, gives the date in Bikram Sambat and AD, and lists each ceremony with its time and venue: often mehendi, haldi, janti, the wedding and the reception or bhoj. Many add a short blessing, a contact number and a map. Nimtto holds all of it in one link.

Every ceremony, one link: Maagni, Mehendi, Haldi, Janti, Swayambar, Kanyadan, Sindoor, Bhitryaune, Preetibhoj.

How it works:
1. Choose a design: Open the preview and see it move. Each design shows the plan it is in.
2. Order and pay: Make your account, then pay by Khalti, eSewa, bank QR, or PayPal from abroad.
3. We make it with you: On WhatsApp: names, dates, venues, photos and your song. You see every change.
4. Share one link: On WhatsApp, Viber or Messenger. Guests open it, see every event and reply.

### What is a maagni?
The maagni (माग्नी) is the Nepali engagement: the day the groom’s family formally asks for the bride’s hand and the two families agree to the marriage.
In many Bahun-Chhetri families, the agreement is sealed with tika, gifts and an exchange of rings (औंठी), followed by a family meal. In Newar families the engagement is often called supari or gwe-biu, after the betel nuts (सुपारी) the groom’s family brings with the ring, as ECS Nepal describes. Today many couples add an engagement party with friends, sometimes on the same day.
The guest list is usually smaller than the wedding’s: both families, close relatives and a few friends. That makes it a good fit for an online card sent straight to each family on WhatsApp.

### What to put on a maagni card
- The couple’s names, with the honorifics your families use

- The date in Bikram Sambat and AD, with the day of the week
- The programme: tika, ring exchange, photos and the meal, each with a time
- The venue, with a map for guests from outside the city
- Who to call with questions
- A reply line, so the meal is planned on real numbers

## Bratabandha Invitation Card Online, Nepali Wording | Nimtto
URL: https://nimtto.com/occasions/bratabandha/
Bratabandha invitation card online in English and Nepali: the full programme, the date in BS and AD, a map and replies. Designed for your family.

Bratabandha invitation cards online.. Bratabandha is the sacred thread ceremony, when a boy receives his janai and his first teaching. We design a bratabandha invitation card online with your son’s name, the full programme from the morning rites to the feast, the date in Bikram Sambat and AD, a map and replies from every guest.

On your bratabandha card:
- Your son’s name: With the parents and family, written the way you want, in Nepali or English.
- The full programme: The morning puja, the rites and the bhoj, each with a time.
- A map: Directions to your home, the temple or the party venue.
- Replies: Numbers for the feast, from relatives near and far.

### What is bratabandha?
Bratabandha (व्रतबन्ध), also called upanayana, is the sacred thread ceremony of many Bahun, Chhetri and other Hindu families in Nepal. A boy receives his janai and the guru mantra, and is welcomed into the duties of adult religious life.
The age varies by family and community. Nepali Wikipedia gives about eight as typical, and other sources describe ceremonies for boys from about five to thirteen; the priest chooses the day from the boy’s birth chart. Newar families hold a related rite, the kayta puja, with its own customs. Families often hold the bratabandha for two brothers, or cousins, on the same day.
#### The rites, in the usual order
1. Chudakarma (चूडाकर्म): the boy’s head is shaved, leaving the tuft (टुप्पी).
2. Puja and the sacred fire, led by the family priest.
3. Guru mantra: the guru whispers the Gayatri mantra to the boy.
4. Janai (जनै): he puts on the sacred thread.
5. Bhiksha (भिक्षा): dressed as a young ascetic with a staff, he asks relatives for alms and sets off as if for the forest; his maternal uncle (mama) brings him back home.
6. Bhoj: the family feast, which most guests attend.
Rites and their order differ between families and priests. Sources: Nepali Wikipedia, व्रतबन्ध and OnlineKhabar on the janai.

### What to put on a bratabandha card
Most guests come for the bhoj in the evening, while close family is there from the morning. A good card makes that clear, so nobody arrives at the wrong time.
- An opening blessing in your family’s style
- The boy’s name (or both brothers’ names) and the parents’ names
- The date in Bikram Sambat and AD, with the day of the week
- The programme with times: chudakarma, guru mantra, bhiksha and the bhoj
- The venue, whether home, a temple or a party venue, with a map
- The mama’s name, if your family includes it
- The hosts after निमन्त्रक and a contact number
- A reply line, with numbers for the bhoj

### Bratabandha card wording (व्रतबन्धको निम्तो)
Nepali, formal:
॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥
हाम्रा सुपुत्र चि. आरवको
चूडाकर्म तथा व्रतबन्ध संस्कारको शुभ अवसरमा
तपाईंको सपरिवार उपस्थितिको कामना गर्दछौं।

मिति: बिहिबार, २८ माघ २०८३
भोज: बेलुका ६ बजेदेखि

हाम्रा सुपुत्रहरू चि. आरव र चि. आयुषको

अवश्य आइदिनुहोला।

### Gunyo cholo: the day a daughter wears her first sari
Gunyo cholo (गुन्यू चोलो), also written gunyu cholo or gunyo choli, marks a girl’s step from childhood towards adulthood. It is often compared with a boy’s bratabandha.
On the day, the girl is dressed in her first gunyu, a sari-like wrap, and a cholo, the fitted blouse. The clothes are traditionally given by her parents and her maternal uncle (mama). Her mother may dress her in jewellery, elders give tika, gifts and cash, and the family shares a meal. Sources put the usual age at about seven to nine, before puberty, though families differ.
Other communities have their own rites for girls. Newar families hold ihi (the bel fruit marriage) and bahra, which are different ceremonies with different invitations. Tell us which rite your family is holding and we word the card to match.
Sources: Wikipedia, Chaubandi cholo and Source Nepal on gunyo cholo.

### What to put on a gunyo cholo card
- Your daughter’s name and the parents’ names
- The date in Bikram Sambat and AD, with the day of the week

- The venue, home or a party venue, with a map
- A photo of her, if you like
- The hosts and a contact number
- A reply line, with numbers for the meal

## Pasni Invitation Card Online in Nepal, With Wording | Nimtto
URL: https://nimtto.com/occasions/pasni/
Pasni (annaprashan) invitation card online: your baby’s name, photos, the date in BS and AD, the feast, a map and replies. In English and Nepali.

Pasni invitation cards online.. Pasni, or annaprashan, is your baby’s first taste of rice, often in the fifth month for a daughter and the sixth or seventh for a son. We design a pasni invitation card online with your baby’s name and photo, the date in Bikram Sambat and AD, the time of the feast, a map and replies from every guest.

On your pasni card:
- Your baby: Name, a photo, and a line from the proud parents.
- The programme: The puja, the first rice and the feast, each with a time.
- A map: Directions for every guest.
- Replies: Numbers for the feast, from near and far.

### What happens at a pasni?
Pasni (पास्नी), or annaprashan (अन्नप्राशन), is a baby’s first meal of rice. Newar families call it macha janko. It is one of the happiest family days of the first year.
The family priest picks an auspicious day, often in the fifth month for a girl and the sixth or seventh for a boy; sources and families differ, so follow your own. After a short puja, the baby is dressed in new clothes and fed a little rice pudding (kheer, खिर), often first by a parent or the eldest relative, then by each relative in turn with tika and blessings. Grandparents often give gold or silver, such as silver anklets.
#### The tray of objects
Many families place a tray in front of the baby with things like a book, a pen, money or jewellery, and a lump of clay or soil. The first thing the baby grabs is said to hint at their future: learning, wisdom, wealth or land. It makes the best photo of the day, and a lovely line for the card after the event.
Sources: Wikipedia, Annaprashana and a family account on Nepali Australian.

### What to put on a pasni card
- Your baby’s name and a photo
- The parents’ names, and grandparents’ if your family likes
- The date in Bikram Sambat and AD, with the day of the week
- The programme: puja, the first rice and the bhoj, each with a time
- The venue, with a map and parking
- A note on lunch or dinner, such as “lunch will be served”
- A reply line, with numbers for the feast

### Pasni card wording (पास्नीको निम्तो)
Nepali, for a son:
हाम्रा छोरा सिद्धार्थको

आशीर्वाद दिन आउनु हुन सादर अनुरोध गर्दछौं।

मिति: शनिबार, १८ बैशाख २०८४
समय: दिउँसो १२ बजेदेखि
भोजनको व्यवस्था गरिएको छ।
Nepali, for a daughter:
हाम्री छोरी मीराको पास्नीको खुसियालीमा
तपाईं सपरिवार पाल्नुहुन
हार्दिक निमन्त्रणा गर्दछौं।

#### When is pasni done for a baby?
Pasni, the rice-feeding ceremony, is often held in the fifth month for a daughter and the sixth or seventh month for a son, on an auspicious day the family priest chooses. Customs differ between families. Relatives feed the baby the first rice and give blessings, then the family shares a feast.

#### What do you write on a pasni invitation card?
Write your baby’s name and the parents’ names, the day in Bikram Sambat and AD, the venue and the time of the feast. Many families add a baby photo and a short blessing. Nimtto sets it in English, Nepali or both, with a map and replies.

## Nwaran Naming Ceremony Invitation Card Online | Nimtto
URL: https://nimtto.com/occasions/nwaran/
Nwaran naming ceremony invitation card online: the new name revealed as guests open it, the date in BS and AD, a map and replies. In English and Nepali.

Nwaran naming ceremony invitation cards.. Nwaran is the naming day, traditionally on the eleventh day after a baby is born. - The programme: The naming puja and the family meal.
- A map: Directions to your home or venue.
- Replies: Who is coming, so you plan the meal right.

### What is a nwaran?
Nwaran (न्वारन) is the Hindu naming ceremony in Nepal, traditionally on the eleventh day after a baby is born. It also ends the period of birth impurity for the mother and the home.
On the day, the house is cleaned and purified, and the family priest works out the baby’s birth chart from the exact time of birth. From it he suggests the first sound of the name, and the family chooses the name. The birth-chart name is not always the name the child uses every day.
A nwaran is usually small: grandparents, close relatives and neighbours, with a family meal afterwards. If the eleventh day is not possible, some families hold it on the 21st or 41st day. A few days earlier, on the sixth night, many families also mark chhaithi (छैटी).
Sources: Wikipedia, Nwaran and Nepali Wikipedia, न्वारन.

### A nwaran card, ready in time
A nwaran leaves very little time: the date depends on the birth, and the family is busy with a newborn. An online card helps because it needs no printing or delivery. Tell us the date when you order and we work around it.
1. Order as soon as you know the day, with the parents’ names, the time and the place.
2. Tell us if the name should be revealed on the card or kept for the day.
3. Approve the design on WhatsApp.

### How Nepali families celebrate birthdays
In many Nepali homes a birthday (जन्मदिन) starts in the morning, not with a cake: a small puja, tika from the elders and their blessings for a long life. The party, with cake and friends, often comes later.
Many families still mark a birthday by the tithi, the lunar day in the Nepali calendar, so the date moves each year against the AD calendar. Others keep the AD date for school friends and the tithi for the family. On a Nimtto card you can show both: the date in Bikram Sambat and in AD, side by side.
Some birthdays are bigger family occasions: a child’s first birthday, a 60th, and the chaurasi at 84. Newar families also have their own birthday customs, like yomari on certain childhood birthdays.
Family customs from a first-hand account on Nepali Australian.

### Chaurasi puja: celebrating 84 years
Reaching 84 is a great blessing, and many families mark it with a chaurasi puja and a gathering of children, grandchildren and relatives. It is often tied to the idea of having seen a thousand full moons (सहस्र चन्द्र दर्शन). The programme usually starts with Vedic rites and a puja in the morning, then tika, blessings and a meal for the whole family.
A chaurasi card is usually sent by the children of the elder. It names the elder with respect, gives the programme by time and invites relatives near and far to come for blessings.

## Janku Invitation Card Online: Bhimratha and More | Nimtto
URL: https://nimtto.com/occasions/janku/
Janku invitation card online for the Newar old-age rites, from Bhimratha at 77: the programme, the date in BS and AD, a map and replies. Designed for you.

Janku invitation cards online.. Janku honours an elder who reaches a great age, a Newar tradition that begins with the Bhimratharohan at 77 years, 7 months and 7 days. We design a janku invitation card online with the elder’s name, the programme, the date in Bikram Sambat, AD and Nepal Sambat if you like, a map and replies.

On your janku card:

- The programme: The rites, the chariot procession and the feast, each with a time.
- A map: Directions to the courtyard or venue.
- Replies: Numbers for the feast, from the whole family.

### The five jankus, and when they are held
Janku (जंकु), or ratharohan, is a Newar rite of old age. Each stage is held at an exact age counted in years, months and days, and each is a reason for the whole family to gather.
The first janku is by far the most common, because it is reached most often. Sources agree on the first age but give slightly different ages for the later stages, so ask your family priest (gubhaju or purohit) for the exact day.
The janku stages
Janku | In Nepali | Age
Bhimratharohan | भीमरथारोहण | 77 years, 7 months, 7 days
Chandraratharohan | चन्द्ररथारोहण | About 82 to 83 years, near a thousand full moons; sources differ
Devaratharohan | देवरथारोहण | 88 years, 8 months, 8 days
Divyaratharohan | दिव्यरथारोहण | 99 years, 9 months, 9 days
Mahadivyaratharohan | महादिव्यरथारोहण | Over 105 years; sources differ
Sources: the Rubin Museum and Nepali Times.

### What happens at a Bhimratha janku
The rites can run over several days with the family priest. On the main day, the elder, dressed in new clothes and often crowned, is seated on a wooden chariot (ratha) and pulled through the neighbourhood by sons, grandchildren and relatives, with music. For a couple, the timing usually follows the husband’s age, and husband and wife ride together. The day ends with a feast for relatives from near and far.
Because the procession has a fixed route and time, the card should say exactly where and when it starts, so relatives can line the way.

### What to put on a janku card
- The elder’s name, with respect, and a photo
- Which janku it is, such as भीमरथारोहण
- The family hosting, usually the sons and their families
- The date in Bikram Sambat and AD, and Nepal Sambat if you like
- The programme: rites, the chariot procession with its start time and route, the feast
- The venue, the courtyard or party venue, with a map
- A reply line, with numbers for the feast

हाम्रा पूज्य बुबा हरि बहादुर महर्जनको
भीमरथारोहण (जंकु) को पावन अवसरमा
सपरिवार उपस्थित भई आशीर्वाद लिनुहुन
सादर निमन्त्रणा गर्दछौं।

भोज: बेलुका ६ बजेदेखि

### Reception, preetibhoj and bhoj: what each one is
A bhoj (भोज) is a feast a family hosts for relatives, neighbours and friends. After a wedding it is called preetibhoj (प्रीतिभोज), the reception, and it is often the event with the biggest guest list.
Families hold the reception in different ways. Some host it on the wedding day, some the day after at the groom’s home or a party palace, and some families hold a separate reception for each side. Many Nepali families feel they must invite every relative, neighbour and friend, which is why numbers matter so much. Weddings and receptions are also moving from homes to party palaces and banquet halls, as Republica has reported, and the venue needs a head count.
A bhoj also follows many other ceremonies: a bratabandha, a pasni, a janku. On all of them, the evening feast is when most guests come.

### Plan the food on real numbers
Party palaces and caterers price by the plate, so a wrong guess costs money either way. An online card with replies gives you a real count instead of a guess.
1. Send the card with a clear reply line, such as “please reply by 15 Magh”.
2. Guests reply on the card with the number of people coming.
3. Your dashboard adds them up; download the list any time.
4. A few days before, call the people who have not replied, and give the caterer your number.

### What to put on a reception card
- The hosts: the couple, or the family, the way you write it
- The occasion, such as preetibhoj after the wedding of…
- The date in Bikram Sambat and AD, with the day of the week
- The time, “from 6 PM” style, as guests come and go
- The venue, with a map and parking notes
- A reply line and the date to reply by
- A contact number for the family

### The events of a Nepali wedding abroad
A Nepali wedding in the USA usually keeps the heart of the rites from home and fits them into a weekend: the maagni or tika, the wedding day itself and a reception for everyone.
The order and the names change from family to family and from priest to priest, and Newar, Bahun-Chhetri, Kirat, Madhesi and other families each keep their own customs. Mehendi and haldi have become popular only recently, as the Kathmandu Post and Republica have both reported. Your designer lists the events exactly as your family holds them.
Events often found on a Nepali wedding invitation
Event | In Nepali | What guests need
Engagement | माग्नी, टीका, औंठी | Date, place, who is hosting
Mehendi | मेहेन्दी | Time, venue, colors to wear
Haldi | हल्दी | Time, and a note to wear old or yellow clothes
Janti (the groom’s procession) | जन्ती | Where to gather and the departure time
Wedding ceremony | शुभ विवाह | The auspicious time (साइत), the venue and a map
Reception or feast | प्रीतिभोज | Time, venue, RSVP numbers for the food

### Two languages and two calendars
Your guests in the USA read English; your grandparents in Nepal may prefer Nepali, and they think in Bikram Sambat (विक्रम सम्वत्), Nepal’s official calendar, which runs about 56 to 57 years ahead of the AD calendar. A Nimtto invitation switches the whole page between English and नेपाली with one tap, and shows the BS date beside the AD date, so everyone reads the same day.
- Names, blessings and event names can be written in Devanagari.
- The BS date can include the day of the week, like शनिबार, १८ मंसिर २०८४.
- Many families open with a short blessing line from their own tradition, set in Devanagari.
- Times show in the venue’s local time, so relatives in Nepal know it is a US time.

### Nepali wedding invitation wording, in English and Nepali
Traditional Nepali cards are sent by the family, not the couple, and end with the hosts’ names after a word like निमन्त्रक or विनीत. Use the samples below as a starting point; your family priest or elders may prefer their own phrasing.
Formal, from the family:
हाम्रा सुपुत्र चि. आरव
र सौ. प्रिया को शुभ विवाहको पावन अवसरमा
तपाईं सपरिवार उपस्थित भइदिनु हुन
हार्दिक निमन्त्रणा गर्दछौं।

निमन्त्रक
शर्मा परिवार
With joy, the Sharma family invites you
and your family to the wedding of
Aarav and Priya.
Reception:
प्रीतिभोज
मिति: शनिबार, १८ मंसिर २०८४
समय: बेलुका ७ बजेदेखि
स्थान: द रिजेन्सी, अर्भिङ, टेक्सस
Reception dinner
Saturday, December 4, 2027 · from 7:00 PM
The Regency, Irving, Texas
English, for friends:
Together with their families
Priya Thapa and Aarav Sharma
invite you to celebrate their wedding
Saturday, December 4, 2027
Irving, Texas
Please see each event below and reply by November 1
Janti departure:
जन्ती प्रस्थान: बिहान ९ बजे
स्थान: शर्मा निवास
The groom’s procession leaves at 9:00 AM
from the Sharma home.
Sample lines follow the common pattern of Nepali wedding cards. The names, places and dates are examples.

### The events of a South Asian wedding, on one invitation
A South Asian wedding is rarely one event. It is a run of celebrations over two to five days, each with its own guest list, dress code and venue. A printed suite handles this with insert cards; a wedding invitation website handles it with one page per event.
Families from different traditions name and order the events differently, so use the list below as a starting point, not a rule. Your designer sets the events in the order your family holds them.
Common events and what guests need to know
Event | What happens | What guests need on the invitation
Engagement or roka | The families formally agree to the match; often a small gathering | Date, place, who is hosting
Mehendi or mehndi | Henna for the bride and guests, music and food | Time, venue, a note on colors to wear
Haldi | Turmeric paste for the couple; a messy, joyful family morning | Wear old clothes or yellow, the time it starts
Sangeet | An evening of music, dance and performances | Dress code, whether guests perform, the venue map
Baraat | The groom’s procession to the venue, with music | Where to gather and when, parking
Wedding ceremony | The main rites, often in the morning or afternoon | Start time, length, dress code, a map
Reception | Dinner and dancing, often the largest guest list | Time, venue, RSVP numbers, meal notes

### Different guest lists for different events
Most families invite close relatives to the mehendi and haldi, a wider circle to the sangeet, and everyone to the ceremony and reception. Planning guides such as Joy’s guide to Indian wedding events recommend a separate yes or no for each event, and showing guests only the events they are invited to.
On Nimtto, every event has its own reply, so you see the numbers for each meal and each bus. On the Pro Max plan, personal guest links open the invitation with the guest’s name and only their events, so nobody sees a party they are not invited to.

### South Asian wedding invitation wording
Many families open with a blessing line from their own tradition, then name the parents as hosts. Keep the main card formal, and give each event a short line of its own.

### When to send a multi-event wedding invitation
Multi-day weddings need more notice than a single ceremony, especially when relatives fly in from overseas and may need visas. Send the save the date early, then the full invitation about three months out.
A timeline for a multi-day South Asian wedding
When | What to do
9 to 12 months before | Save the date to family abroad, so they can plan visas and leave
4 to 6 months before | Save the date to everyone, mentioning that there are several events
About 3 months before | The full invitation with every event, dress codes and the RSVP
About 6 weeks before | RSVP deadline for every event
About 4 weeks before | Final numbers per event to caterers, decorators and transport
Visa wait times change. Families inviting relatives from abroad should check current times on the US Department of State’s visa site early.

### Digital or printed invitations for a South Asian wedding?

Many families now send the digital invitation to everyone and give a small number of printed cards by hand to elders. The digital one does what paper cannot: maps, live updates, a separate RSVP for each event and family overseas on the same link.

### What your guests see when they reply
An RSVP link only works if replying is easier than ignoring it. Guests should be able to answer on the screen they opened the invitation on, without logging in.
There is no app, no account and no password, which matters most for older relatives and guests overseas. If a guest changes their mind, they can reply again and you see the latest answer.
1. They tap your link in a text, an email or WhatsApp. The invitation opens in their browser.
2. They watch the short opening, then scroll through the events, the map and the travel notes.
3. At the reply form they type their name and say yes or no to each event.
4. They add how many people are coming, a meal choice if you asked for one, and an optional note.
5. They tap send. Their reply lands in your dashboard straight away.

### What to ask on a wedding RSVP form
Ask only what you will use. Every extra question makes a guest more likely to stop halfway. These are the questions couples use most.
- Attending or not, for each event they are invited to.
- Number of guests, so you can match it to who you invited.
- Meal choice, if your caterer needs it in advance.
- Dietary needs or allergies, as a short note.
- Song request or a note for the couple, which guests enjoy.
- Travel details, such as arrival day, only if you plan shuttles.

### When to set your RSVP deadline
Most planners set the RSVP date three to four weeks before the wedding. That gives you time to chase late replies, give your caterer final numbers and make a seating chart. For a destination or multi-day wedding, ask earlier, around six weeks out, because hotel blocks and transport need numbers sooner.
RSVP timing for a wedding
Wedding type | Send the invitation | RSVP by
Local wedding | 6 to 8 weeks before | 3 to 4 weeks before
Destination wedding | 10 to 12 weeks before | About 6 weeks before
Multi-day wedding with several events | About 3 months before | 4 to 6 weeks before, for every event
Small wedding at short notice | 3 to 4 weeks before | 1 to 2 weeks before
These are common ranges from wedding planning guides; your venue and caterer’s deadlines come first.

### RSVP wording for your invitation
The RSVP line tells guests how and by when to reply. On a digital invitation it sits right above the form, so it can be short.
Formal:
The favour of a reply is requested
by the first of May
Classic:
Kindly reply by May 1
We have reserved two seats in your honor
Relaxed:
Let us know if you can make it by May 1.
Tap below to reply for each event.
A gentle reminder:
Hi Sam, a quick reminder to reply for our wedding by Friday.
It takes a minute: [your link]

### How to handle guests who have not replied
Every wedding has late replies. Your dashboard shows who has answered, so you only remind the people who have not.
- Send a short, friendly reminder a few days before the RSVP date, with the same link.
- Ask a parent or a friend to call the relatives who rarely use email.
- After the deadline, count non-replies as “not attending” for planning, then confirm by phone if the number matters.
- Never ask guests to reply on two systems. One link keeps the count right.

### Online RSVP vs reply cards
Ways to collect wedding RSVPs
 | RSVP on the invitation link | Mailed reply card | Text or phone
Effort for guests | About a minute, on their phone | Fill, stamp and post | Easy, but answers get lost in chats
Per-event answers | Yes, for each event | Only if the card lists them | Hard to track
Meal choices | Collected with the reply | Tick boxes on the card | Easy to forget
Your guest list | Updates itself; download any time | Typed in by hand | Typed in by hand
Cost | Included in your plan | Printing and return postage | Free, but slow

Yes. Download every reply as a spreadsheet at any time, with names, events, numbers and meal choices. Use it for your caterer, your seating chart, your hotel block or your thank-you notes.

#### Can guests reply to some events and not others?
Yes. Each event has its own yes or no, so a guest can come to the ceremony and reception but skip the welcome drinks. On the Pro Max plan, personal guest links can also show each guest only the events they are invited to.

#### Can a guest change their reply?
Yes. A guest can open the same link and reply again, and your dashboard shows their latest answer. If plans change close to the day, ask guests to message you as well, so your caterer hears in time.

#### How do I stop people bringing extra guests?
Address the invitation to the people you are inviting and ask for the number of guests on the form. Your list shows each reply’s number, so you can follow up kindly if it is more than you planned. Personal links on Pro Max make this easier.

#### Is there a fee per guest?
No. You pay once for your plan, from $49, and can invite as many guests as you like. There is no subscription and no charge per reply.

#### Is my guests’ information private?
Yes. Replies are shown only to you and our team, and we use them only to run your invitation. We never sell your data, and you can ask us to delete it at any time.

#### What RSVP deadline should I set?
Three to four weeks before a local wedding, and about six weeks before a destination or multi-day wedding. Check your caterer’s and venue’s deadlines first, then set yours a few days earlier.

### What is a digital wedding invitation?
A digital wedding invitation is an invitation your guests open on a phone or computer instead of in the mail. The best ones do more than paper can: they hold the schedule, the maps, the hotel block and the RSVP in the same link.
With Nimtto, the link first plays a short opening, like a wax seal breaking or an arch of roses parting, and then your names appear. Below it sits your wedding website: every event with its time and place, travel notes, your story, photos, your song and the reply form. Guests do not download an app or make an account.
It is not a template you fill in alone. You choose a design, and a real designer sets it up with you by email or WhatsApp. You check every change before any guest sees it, and you can still edit times and places after you send it.

### What to include on a wedding invitation
Every wedding invitation answers the same questions: who is getting married, who is hosting, when, where and how to reply. A digital invitation has room for the rest, so the card itself can stay clean and formal while the details sit one scroll below.
- The hosts. Your parents, both families, or the two of you.
- The request line. For example “request the pleasure of your company”.
- Both full names, in the order your families prefer.
- The date and time, written out on formal invitations.
- The ceremony venue with its city, and a map for every stop.
- The reception, if it is at another time or place.
- The RSVP date and method. With Nimtto, guests reply on the invitation.
- Your wedding website details: dress code, travel, hotels, children and plus-ones.
Etiquette writers such as the Emily Post Institute suggest keeping the registry off the invitation itself and on the wedding website instead. On Nimtto it sits in its own section, below the events.

“The honour of your presence” is the traditional line for a ceremony in a house of worship, and “the pleasure of your company” for any other venue, as the Emily Post Institute explains.

### When to send wedding invitations
Most planning guides agree on six to eight weeks before the wedding for the invitation itself, with the RSVP date three to four weeks before the day. Guests who must travel need more notice, which is what the save the date is for. Sources differ a little on save the dates: the Emily Post Institute suggests three to six months, while Zola suggests seven to ten, and ten to twelve for a destination wedding.
A wedding invitation timeline
When | What to send or do
8 to 12 months before | Destination or multi-day wedding: send a save the date so guests can book flights and leave.
4 to 8 months before | Local wedding: send a save the date with the date and city.
10 to 12 weeks before | Destination wedding: send the invitation, with hotel and travel details.
6 to 8 weeks before | Send the invitation. With Nimtto it is the same link, now with every detail and the RSVP.
3 to 4 weeks before | RSVP deadline. You can see who has not replied and send them a reminder.
1 to 2 weeks before | Give final numbers and meal choices to your caterer from your guest list download.
The week of the wedding | Update anything that changed, like a shuttle time. Everyone with the link sees it.

### Is it okay to send wedding invitations by text or email?
For most couples, yes. Opinions do differ, and it is worth knowing both sides. Traditional etiquette, like the Emily Post Institute’s advice, still prefers a printed invitation for a formal wedding. Planning sites such as Zola call it a personal choice, and many couples now go digital for everyone or nearly everyone.
A digital invitation feels right when it looks like it was made for your wedding, not pulled from a free template. Write it with the same care as a printed card, send it personally rather than as a mass email, and follow up with guests who have not opened it.
#### The middle path most couples choose
Send the digital invitation to everyone, and post a few printed cards to grandparents or anyone who would treasure one. Ask a relative to help older guests open the link and reply. You keep one guest list and one set of replies.

### Keeping a surprise party a surprise
A surprise party fails in one of two ways: someone mentions it, or guests arrive after the guest of honor. A private invitation link helps with both.
- Send the link only to guests, never to a shared family group the guest of honor is in.
- Put “It’s a surprise” at the top, where nobody can miss it.
- Give guests an arrival time 30 minutes before the guest of honor arrives.
- Add parking notes, so a row of familiar cars outside does not give it away.
- Use the RSVP list to know exactly who will be there for the big moment.

### A note on kids’ party guest lists
Etiquette writers such as the Emily Post Institute suggest inviting the whole class or team, or only a few close friends, so no child feels left out, and not handing invitations out at school. A link sent to parents solves the second point neatly: invitations go straight to the families you choose.

### Who hosts a baby shower, and who sends the invitation
Traditionally a close friend or a relative outside the immediate family hosted the shower, so it did not look like the parents were asking for gifts. Today etiquette is more relaxed: the Emily Post Institute says anyone may host when there is a good reason, and co-hosting by friends, sisters, grandmothers or coworkers is common.
The host sends the invitation and collects the replies. With a link, two or three co-hosts can share the same invitation and all see the guest list.
#### Shower, sprinkle or co-ed?
- Baby shower: the classic party before a first baby, often with games, food and gifts.
- Sprinkle: a smaller, lighter party for a second or later baby, often with diapers or books instead of big gifts.
- Co-ed shower: partners and friends of every kind are invited, so the guest list is often larger.
- Meet-the-baby party: held after the birth, when the family is ready for visitors.

### When to send baby shower invitations
Send baby shower invitations four to six weeks before the shower and ask for replies about a week before. Guides vary a little: Evite suggests up to six to eight weeks, and the Emily Post Institute three to six. Many showers are held four to eight weeks before the due date, when the parent-to-be still feels like a party.
A baby shower timeline
When | What to do
8 to 10 weeks before the shower | Agree on the date, the hosts and the guest list with the parents-to-be
6 weeks before | Set up the registry, so you can link to it
4 to 6 weeks before | Send the invitation link
1 week before | RSVP deadline; give the venue or caterer the numbers
After the shower | Add a few photos to the same link for family who could not come

### What goes on a baby shower invitation
- The parent or parents-to-be, and the baby’s name if it is shared
- The hosts’ names
- Date, time and place, with a map and parking
- The theme or dress code, if there is one
- Registry details, or a note like “books instead of cards”
- The RSVP date, with replies on the invitation
- A link for family far away to join by video
Is the registry okay on a shower invitation? Showers are a gift-giving party, so most modern guides say yes; a short line or link in the details is fine. On a wedding invitation it is not.

### Baby shower invitation wording
Classic:
Please join us for a baby shower
honoring Olivia Grant

#### What goes on a baby shower invitation?
A baby shower invitation names the parents-to-be and the host, then gives the date, time and place, with a map. Most add an RSVP date, a note about gifts or the registry, and any theme or dress code. We put all of it in one link guests can open anywhere.

#### When should I send baby shower invitations?
Send baby shower invitations about four to six weeks before the shower, and ask guests to reply a week before. With an online invitation you send it in minutes, change the details if plans move, and see every reply as it comes in.

#### When should I send baby shower invitations?
Send them four to six weeks before the shower and ask for replies about a week before. If many guests travel, send them closer to eight weeks ahead. An online invitation goes out in minutes and you can change the details if plans move.

#### Can I add a registry link?
Yes. Add a note with a link to your registry, or ask guests for books instead of cards. Showers are a gift-giving party, so a short registry line is widely accepted. It is your invitation and your words.

#### Who should host a baby shower?
Traditionally a close friend or relative outside the immediate family, but today anyone may host, including grandmothers, sisters, coworkers or several friends together. The host sends the invitation and collects the replies, which is easy to share on one link.

#### How many people should I invite?
There is no fixed number. Invite the people the parents-to-be would want around them, and remember that a co-ed shower often doubles the list. Your reply list shows the exact count, so you can plan food and seating on real numbers.

#### Can family far away join?
Yes. Add a video call or live stream link so family far away can watch the games and the gifts being opened. The invitation opens anywhere in the world, so relatives overseas see the time and can reply.

#### Can you design a gender reveal invitation?
Yes. We design gender reveal invitations, and the design can keep the secret until the party. Tell us the colors and the idea, and we make an invitation with the date, the place and an RSVP.

## Bridal Shower Invitation Online With RSVP | Nimtto
URL: https://nimtto.com/international/occasions/bridal-shower/
Bridal shower invitation online, designed for you: brunch, games and gifts in one link, with a map, a registry note and RSVP. Custom from $199.

Bridal shower invitations online, with RSVP.. Brunch, games, gifts and the bride-to-be: we design a bridal shower invitation online with the date, the place, a map, a registry note and an RSVP, in one link the maid of honor can send by text or email. It can match the wedding invitation, too.

On your bridal shower invitation:
- Hosted by: The maid of honor, the family or friends, named the way you want.
- The details: Brunch time, place, a map and a theme or dress code.
- Registry note: Where to find the registry, or a recipe to bring.
- RSVP: Know the numbers for the table.

### Bridal shower etiquette: who hosts and who is invited
A bridal shower is hosted for the bride (or the couple) by the people closest to her. The Emily Post Institute says anyone may host except the couple themselves, and that the maid of honor is not obliged to. Sisters, mothers, aunts, friends and bridesmaids often share the hosting.
#### The guest list rule
Invite only people who are also invited to the wedding. A shower is a gift-giving party, so asking someone to celebrate and bring a gift without a wedding invitation feels unfair. The one common exception is an office shower thrown by coworkers.
#### When to hold it
Most showers fall between two months and two weeks before the wedding. Earlier, and the registry may not be ready; later, and the bride has no time to breathe.

### When to send bridal shower invitations
Send bridal shower invitations four to six weeks before the shower, and about two months ahead for guests who must travel. Ask for replies one to two weeks before, so the host can confirm the brunch numbers. The Knot and Paperless Post both suggest this range.
A bridal shower timeline
When | What to do
3 months before the wedding | Choose the hosts, the date and the guest list with the bride
8 weeks before the shower | Send to out-of-town guests, or share a save the date
4 to 6 weeks before | Send the invitation to everyone
1 to 2 weeks before | RSVP deadline; confirm the numbers with the venue
2 weeks to 2 months before the wedding | The shower itself

### What to put on a bridal shower invitation
- The bride’s name (or both names for a couples’ shower)
- Who is hosting
- Date and time, and roughly how long it lasts
- The place, with a map and parking
- The theme or dress code, such as garden tea party or brunch
- Registry information, or what to bring for a recipe or lingerie shower
- The RSVP date and who to ask
Showers are the one wedding event where a registry line is widely accepted on the invitation. Keep it to one short line or link.

The host sends it, usually a sister, the mother of the bride, close friends or the bridesmaids, not the bride herself. With an online invitation, the host sends one link by text or email and sees every reply, and co-hosts can share the guest list.

URL: https://nimtto.com/international/occasions/engagement-party/

Engagement party invitations to share the news.. You said yes, now tell everyone. We design an engagement party invitation online with your names, the date, the place, a map and an RSVP, in one link you send by text or email. Later, your wedding invitation can keep the same look.

On your engagement invitation:

- Party details and a map: Date, time, place and parking, in one link.
- RSVP with numbers: See who is coming and how many.

### Who hosts an engagement party?
Traditionally the bride’s parents hosted the first engagement party, with the groom’s family sometimes hosting a second. Today the couple, either set of parents, or close friends all host, and many couples hold one relaxed party for both families. The Emily Post Institute notes that whoever hosts sends the invitation.
#### The one guest list rule
Everyone invited to the engagement party should also be invited to the wedding. If you are not sure yet how big the wedding will be, keep the engagement party small: close family and friends you know you will invite.

### When to send engagement party invitations
Send engagement party invitations two to six weeks before the party. Two to four weeks suits a casual party at home; four to six weeks suits a larger party at a venue or one with guests traveling in. Most engagement parties happen within the first few months after the proposal, before wedding planning takes over.
An engagement party timeline
When | What to do
1 to 3 months after the proposal | Pick a date and the hosts
4 to 6 weeks before | Send the invitation for a larger party or traveling guests
2 to 4 weeks before | Send the invitation for a casual party
1 to 2 weeks before | RSVP deadline; confirm food and drink numbers

### What to include on an engagement party invitation
- Both names, in the order you like
- Who is hosting
- Date and time
- The place, with a map and parking
- Dress code, such as cocktail or backyard casual
- The RSVP date
- A photo of the two of you, if you like
Gifts are not expected at an engagement party, so leave the registry off the invitation. If guests ask, the wedding website can answer later.

### Anniversary milestones and their traditional names
The big anniversaries have traditional names and materials, which make an easy theme for the invitation and the party. These are the names most often used in the USA and the UK.
Traditional anniversary names
Year | Traditional name | Theme ideas for the invitation

### Who hosts an anniversary party?
For the 25th and especially the 50th, the couple’s children often host, sometimes as a surprise. For other years, the couple usually hosts their own dinner or party. A vow renewal is almost always hosted by the couple, with a structure close to a wedding invitation.
#### Inviting the original wedding party
For a 50th, many families track down the bridesmaids, the best man and old friends from the wedding. Put the original wedding date and place on the invitation; guests love the detail.

Ranges follow Paperless Post’s timing guide; the Emily Post Institute suggests three to six weeks for most parties.

### Graduation announcement vs graduation party invitation
They are two different things. A graduation announcement shares the news that someone has graduated; it carries no obligation to attend or to send a gift, and it can go to a wide circle of family and friends. A graduation party invitation asks people to come to a celebration, so it needs a date, a place and an RSVP.
Many families send both, or combine them: one link that shares the news with a photo for everyone, and the party details for the people invited.

### When to send graduation party invitations
Send graduation party invitations three to four weeks before the party, and about six weeks ahead for guests who travel. In May and June, many families compete for the same weekends, so earlier is better. Evite also suggests a save the date in peak season.
A graduation party timeline
When | What to do
2 to 3 months before | Pick the date, after checking the ceremony schedule
6 weeks before | Send to out-of-town family, or share a save the date
3 to 4 weeks before | Send the invitation to everyone
1 week before | RSVP deadline; order food on real numbers
Graduation day | Add the ceremony live stream link for family far away

### What goes on a graduation party invitation
- The graduate’s full name and a photo
- The school, the degree and the year
- Who is hosting, usually the parents or the graduate
- The date and the time, or an open-house window
- The place, with a map and parking
- The RSVP date
- A ceremony live stream link, if there is one
Etiquette writers such as the Emily Post Institute advise against registries or wish lists on graduation invitations.

#### What is the difference between an announcement and an invitation?
An announcement shares the news and asks nothing of the guest. An invitation asks guests to come to a party, so it has a date, a place and an RSVP. One Nimtto link can do both: the news and photo for everyone, the party details for those invited.

## Digital Housewarming Invitation With RSVP | Nimtto
URL: https://nimtto.com/international/occasions/housewarming/
A digital housewarming invitation with RSVP: your new address with a map, parking notes and the party time in one link. Designed for you, from $199.

Housewarming invitations, with a map to your door.. New keys, new address, an open door: we design a digital housewarming invitation with your new address and a map, parking notes, the party time and an RSVP, in one link you send by text or email. Guests find you the first time.

On your housewarming invitation:
- Your new address: With a map, so guests find you the first time.
- Parking and entry: Where to park, which door, the gate code.
- RSVP: Know the numbers for food and drinks.
- House photos: A peek at the new place.

### When to have a housewarming party, and when to invite
Most people host a housewarming within the first few months after moving in, once the boxes are gone and the living room has somewhere to sit. There is no deadline; a housewarming six months later is still a housewarming.
A housewarming timeline
When | What to do
1 to 3 months after moving in | Pick a date and decide: a set start time or an open house
2 to 3 weeks before | Send the invitation with the new address and a map
3 to 4 weeks before | Send it earlier if guests travel or it falls near a holiday
About 1 week before | RSVP deadline; plan food and drinks
Timing follows common party guides such as Greenvelope’s housewarming wording guide.

### What a housewarming invitation should include
Your guests have never been to this address, which makes the practical details more important than on almost any other invitation.
- Who is hosting, with everyone who lives there
- The new address on its own line, with a map
- Parking: the street, the driveway or the visitor spaces
- How to get in: the gate code, the buzzer, which door
- A set start time, or an open-house window
- Kids and pets: welcome or not, and whether you have a dog
- A gift note, if you want one
- The RSVP date

### Housewarming gift etiquette
Guests are not obliged to bring anything to a housewarming, though many bring a small gift like a plant, a bottle or something to eat. Etiquette writers such as the Emily Post Institute advise against a housewarming registry. If you would rather nobody brought anything, say it kindly in one line.

Sunday, November 7

Please don’t bring anything but yourselves.
We have finally unpacked enough plates.
Apartment:
Buzz 4B at the side entrance.
The elevator is on the left.
Visitor parking is behind the building.

### Keeping your new address private
A housewarming invitation shares your home address, so it should not be public. A Nimtto invitation is only seen by people who have the link: it is not listed anywhere, and you choose who gets it. Send it to guests directly rather than posting it on social media, and ask guests not to forward it. On the Pro Max plan, each guest can have a personal link.

#### When should you have a housewarming party?
Most people host a housewarming within the first few months after moving in, once the boxes are unpacked. Send invitations two to three weeks before. An online invitation with a map helps guests find a new address they have never been to.

Include who is hosting, the new address with a map, the date and time, parking notes and how to RSVP. Many add a line like “no gifts needed” or a wish list. We design it with your words and a photo of the house.

#### When should you have a housewarming party?
Most people host a housewarming within the first few months after moving in, once the boxes are unpacked. Send invitations two to three weeks before, or three to four if guests travel. An online invitation with a map helps guests find an address they have never been to.

#### What should a housewarming invitation include?
Include who is hosting, the new address with a map, the date and time, parking and entry notes and how to RSVP. Many add a line like “no gifts needed” or mention pets. We design it with your words and a photo of the house.

#### Should I host an open house or a set time?
An open house, with a window like 2:00 to 6:00 PM, suits a large or mixed guest list and lets people come and go. A set time suits a dinner or a smaller party. Either works on the invitation, and the RSVP shows roughly how many to expect.

#### Do guests bring gifts to a housewarming?
They are not obliged to, but many bring something small, like a plant, a candle or a bottle. A registry is not usual for a housewarming. If you would prefer no gifts, one friendly line on the invitation does it.

### Rehearsal dinner invitations: who to invite
The rehearsal dinner happens the night before the wedding, after the ceremony rehearsal. It was traditionally hosted by the groom’s parents; today the couple or either family often hosts. The usual guest list:
- The wedding party and their partners
- Both sets of parents and immediate family
- The officiant and their partner
- Parents of any flower girls or ring bearers
- Out-of-town guests, if you choose to include them
#### When to send it
Send rehearsal dinner invitations after the wedding invitations, about three to six weeks before. Guests who see the rehearsal dinner first may wonder if they are invited to the wedding. If your wedding invitation is a Nimtto link, the rehearsal dinner can be one more event on it, shown only to the guests who are invited.
