## Bratabandha Invitation: Customs, Timeline and Wording
URL: https://nimtto.com/blog/bratabandha-invitation-guide/
By Nimtto Team · Published 2026-10-18 · Updated 2026-10-18
What happens at a bratabandha, how the priest's sait sets your invitation timeline, and copy-ready Nepali and English wording for the card and WhatsApp.

A bratabandha invitation card should name the boy as your son, give the ceremony date in Bikram Sambat with the AD date beside it, list the times for the rites and the bhoj, and give the venue with a contact person. The date comes from your priest's sait, so fix that first, book the venue, and send invitations about three to four weeks before the day.

This guide explains the bratabandha ceremony in plain words, shows how the sait shapes your timeline, and gives copy-ready Nepali and English wording. If you want to see an online version first, open our bratabandha invitation page.

What the bratabandha ceremony is

Bratabandha is the Nepali form of upanayana, the sacred thread rite. Britannica describes upanayana as an initiation that marks a boy's entry into student life, with a sacred thread and the Gayatri mantra at its centre. It is often called a second birth.

In Nepal, the rite brings two steps together. The Wikipedia entry on upanayana notes that bratabandha combines chudakarma (head shaving) with the thread ceremony, followed by a first alms round to relatives. For the family, it is one of the biggest days in a son's childhood.

Ages vary by text and by family. Britannica gives a classical range of roughly 5 to 24, while a scholar interviewed by PBS Religion and Ethics says the rite usually happens between 8 and 16 and ideally takes two days. Your priest and elders will guide you on what your family follows.

Customs differ between communities and families. Newar Buddhist families of the Shakya and Bajracharya communities hold their own bratabandha, in which boys shave their heads and dress as monks, as Gulf Times reported. Use this guide as a starting point and follow your own family's practice.

The main rites of the day

Knowing the order of the rites helps you write the programme on the card. Guests want to know when to arrive for the parts they care about, usually the bhiksha and the blessings.

Chudakarma: the first head shave

The day usually starts with chudakarma. The boy's head is shaved, and a small tuft (tuppi) is left at the crown. A Tips Nepal guide to bratabandha describes the boy's sisters receiving the hair on a plate before it is wrapped and kept aside.

Wearing the janai

Next the boy receives the janai, the sacred thread. Britannica describes it as a loop of three twisted cotton strands, worn over the left shoulder and across the chest.
Receiving the Gayatri mantra

The guru, usually the family priest, then gives the boy the Gayatri mantra. The Tips Nepal guide describes the guru whispering it under a cloth so that no one else hears, and the boy repeating it. In the PBS interview, the boy is then asked to chant the mantra at least three times a day.

Bhiksha from the mother and relatives

The bhiksha is often the most emotional moment. The boy, now a student, asks for alms. Tips Nepal lists the mother first, then grandmothers, sisters, aunts and other relatives, with the maternal uncle walking beside him. The alms are later offered to the guru.

The mama's role and the symbolic journey

The maternal uncle (mama) has a special place. In the step Tips Nepal calls the journey (deshantar), the boy sets out as if to leave home and study far away, often just a short walk to a nearby temple. His mama guides him and persuades him to come back and live with his family.

How the sait shapes your invitation timeline

Everything on the card depends on the sait (also written sahit), the auspicious date and time. Your priest or family astrologer works it out from the boy's birth chart and the panchanga. The panchanga is the same almanac used for wedding dates, and Onlinekhabar explains that the Nepal Panchanga Nirnayak Samiti decides festival dates and auspicious times nationally.

Some families pick Shree Panchami instead. The Rising Nepal notes that the day is regarded as auspicious for functions like marriage and bratabandha. Popular days fill venues and priests quickly, so book early.

Bratabandha celebrations have also grown. Republica reported that many families now host bratabandha parties on the scale of a wedding. A bigger guest list means you need more lead time and a clear way to count who is coming.

A bratabandha invitation timeline

This is a practical plan, counted back from the sait. Adjust it if your priest gives you a date at short notice.

| When | What to do | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| As early as possible | Ask the priest for the sait and confirm the time of the rites | Every other date depends on it |
| Within a week of the sait | Book the venue, cook or caterer, and the barber if needed | Popular days book out |
| Same week | Call the mama's family, grandparents and relatives abroad | They have roles, or need time to travel |
| 3 to 4 weeks before | Send the bratabandha invitation card to everyone | Gives guests time to plan |
| 1 to 2 weeks before | Count RSVPs and give the caterer a number | Avoids too much or too little food |
| 2 to 3 days before | Send a short reminder with the map link | People forget times and turns |
| On the morning | Share the venue location with anyone running late | Saves phone calls during the rites |

If relatives live abroad, give them the date the moment the sait is fixed. Our guide for families abroad explains how they can follow along and reply from wherever they are.

Invite the mama and maiju in person or by phone before you send the card. He has a part in the bhiksha and the journey, so he should hear the date from you first, not from a group message.

What to include on a bratabandha invitation card

Keep the card simple. These are the details guests look for:

1. An invocation such as ॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥, if your family uses one.
2. The heading: शुभ व्रतबन्ध (many cards also write ब्रतबन्ध).
3. The parents' names and the boy's name, with चि. before it.
4. The date in BS first, with the AD date beside it.
5. A short programme: rites, bhiksha and blessings, bhoj.
6. The venue with a map link, or the home address.
7. The family names at the bottom, a contact person and an RSVP date.

The structure follows a Nepali wedding card closely. Our wedding invitation wording guide explains each part in more detail, including honorifics and BS dates.

Bratabandha card matter in Nepali

These blocks use हजुर and honorific verbs throughout. The sample date, वि.सं. २०८३ माघ ८ गते शुक्रबार, matches Friday 22 January 2027. Replace it with your own sait and check the conversion against your patro.

Formal Nepali bratabandha invitation from the parents:
॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥

शुभ व्रतबन्ध

हाम्रा सुपुत्र चि. [छोराको नाम]को व्रतबन्ध (चूडाकर्म तथा उपनयन) संस्कार मिति २०८३ साल माघ ८ गते शुक्रबार शुभ साइतमा सम्पन्न हुने भएकाले उक्त शुभ अवसरमा हजुर सपरिवार उपस्थित भई चिरञ्जीवीलाई शुभ आशीर्वाद दिनुहुन हार्दिक अनुरोध गर्दछौं।

कार्यक्रम
चूडाकर्म तथा व्रतबन्ध संस्कार: बिहान ७:०० बजेदेखि
भिक्षा तथा आशीर्वाद: दिउँसो १२:०० बजे
प्रीतिभोज: बेलुका ५:०० बजेदेखि

स्थान: [घर वा भेन्यूको नाम], [ठेगाना]

दर्शनाभिलाषी
[हजुरबुबा तथा हजुरआमाको नाम]
[बुबा तथा आमाको नाम] सपरिवार
सम्पर्क: [फोन नम्बर]

Short Nepali bratabandha invitation:
शुभ व्रतबन्ध

हाम्रा छोरा चि. [छोराको नाम]को व्रतबन्ध २०८३ माघ ८ गते शुक्रबार हुँदै छ।

यस शुभ दिनमा हजुरको उपस्थिति र आशीर्वादको अपेक्षा गर्दछौं।

स्थान: [भेन्यूको नाम], [ठेगाना]
प्रीतिभोज: बेलुका ५:०० बजेदेखि

[बुबा तथा आमाको नाम] परिवार

A personal note for the mama and maiju:
आदरणीय मामा तथा माइजू,
[छोराको नाम]को व्रतबन्ध २०८३ माघ ८ गते शुक्रबार हुने भएको छ।
भिक्षा र देशान्तरमा हजुरहरूको साथ चाहिन्छ, त्यसैले बिहान ७:०० बजेअघि नै पाल्नुहोला।
[नाम] परिवार

Bratabandha invitation wording in English

English versions help younger guests, colleagues and relatives abroad. Put the BS date in brackets after the AD date.

Our son [Boy's name]'s Bratabandha is on Friday, 22 January 2027 (Magh 8, 2083). Here is our invitation: [link]
The times, venue and map are all on the page. Please reply there by [date]. We hope you can come and bless him.
[Name] family

Reminder two days before:
नमस्ते! [छोराको नाम]को व्रतबन्ध पर्सि शुक्रबार हो। भोज बेलुका ५:०० बजेदेखि छ। नक्सा यहाँ छ: [लिंक]
A gentle reminder: the Bratabandha is this Friday, with the bhoj from 5:00 pm. Map: [link]

Choosing a design for a family ceremony

A bratabandha card should feel festive and rooted, not like a wedding card with the names changed. Designs built around doors, windows and marigolds suit a family ceremony at home well.

On Nimtto, Mangal opens a red temple door with bells, Sayapatri hangs marigold strings in a doorway, and Jhyal frames your wording in a carved Newari window.

Phone screen showing the Mangal invitation, a red temple door with hanging bells

Each event can have its own time and map, guests reply on the invitation, and you see the count in your dashboard. The same setup works for other family rites, such as a pasni or a daughter's gunyu cholo. Our pasni invitation guide has wording for that one too.

Before you send

Read the card once more for the details families most often get wrong: the boy's name spelling, the BS and AD dates, the bhoj time and the venue. Ask an elder to check the Nepali, and make sure the mama's family heard the news from you first.

When the wording is ready, a Nimtto designer can set it up in Nepali and English and review it with you before any guest sees it. Start from the bratabandha invitation page, see how it works, or compare plans on the pricing page.

### At what age is bratabandha done?
There is no single age. Classical texts and family custom differ, and many Nepali families hold it while the boy is still a child or a young teenager, on a date their priest chooses.

### Is chudakarma the same as bratabandha?
Not exactly. Chudakarma is the head-shaving rite. In Nepal it is usually done on the same day, as the first part of the bratabandha, before the boy receives the janai.

### How many days before a bratabandha should we send invitations?
Three to four weeks is a comfortable window for guests in Nepal. Tell close family and relatives abroad as soon as the sait is fixed, then send the full invitation later.

### Who is named as the host on a bratabandha card?
The boy's parents send it, and the grandparents or the head of the family are often listed at the bottom with सपरिवार. The boy is named as their son, usually with चि. before his name.

### Do guests bring gifts to a bratabandha?
Relatives often give money or gifts during the bhiksha or when they bless the boy. The card itself does not need to mention gifts.

### Can a bratabandha be held on Shree Panchami without a separate sait?
Some families choose Shree Panchami because it is widely treated as an auspicious day for rites like bratabandha. Ask your priest whether it suits your son's chart before you book a venue.

### Can we send a bratabandha invitation online?
Yes. An online invitation can hold the ceremony and bhoj times, a map and RSVP. See the [bratabandha invitation page](/occasions/bratabandha/) for how one looks.

## Digital vs Printed Wedding Cards in Nepal: Cost, Etiquette and What Families Prefer
URL: https://nimtto.com/blog/digital-vs-printed-wedding-cards-nepal/
By Nimtto Team · Published 2026-10-18 · Updated 2026-10-18
An honest look at printed cards and online invitations for a Nepali wedding: what each really costs, what elders expect, and how to send a link without seeming careless.

For most Nepali weddings today, the best answer is not one or the other. The digital wedding card Nepal couples now send on WhatsApp is cheaper per guest, reaches relatives abroad on the same day, and collects RSVPs for you. A printed card still carries weight with elders, who often expect a card in hand or a personal visit.

So many families now do both. They print a small number of cards for grandparents and senior relatives, and send a link to everyone else. This guide compares the two honestly, explains what really drives the cost, and gives you messages you can copy.

E-Card vs Printed Card: The Quick Comparison

Here is how the two options compare on the things families ask about most.

| Point | Printed card | Digital wedding card |
|---|---|---|
| Main cost drivers | Paper, printing method, foil or embossing, boxes, quantity, extra prints, delivery trips | One fixed price for the design and setup; no cost per guest |
| Time to prepare | Design, proof, print run, then days of distribution | Usually 1 to 3 business days of design help, then sent in minutes |
| Reach abroad | Post or courier, slow and costly | Same day, any country, through WhatsApp, Viber or email |
| RSVP | Phone calls and memory | Guests reply on the invitation; you see a list |
| Changes after sending | Reprint, or call everyone | Update once; the same link shows the new details |
| Every ceremony and map | Limited by card size | Each event with time, venue and a Google Maps link |
| Keepsake value | High; it can go in an album | Lower; it lives on a phone |
| How elders feel | Familiar and respectful | Fine for many, if you also call |

Neither option wins every row. That is why the mixed approach, covered below, is so common.

Printed Wedding Card Price in Nepal: What Drives the Cost

You will not find one fixed printed wedding card price in Nepal, because every order is different. One Nepali wedding directory, Bihebazaar, says card prices start from about Rs 50 per card and can go to Rs 500 or more. It names design, printing technique, paper quality and the number of cards as the main factors.

Treat that as a rough range, not a quote. Prices change every season, so ask two or three printers for a written quote on the same specification.

Paper, print and finish

Paper is the first big choice. The Kathmandu Post reported that many Nepali families prefer cards made of traditional lokta paper. Handmade paper, velvet or thick card stock all cost more than plain art paper.

Finishes add to the price. Gold foil, embossing, laser cuts, ribbons and wax seals each add a step at the press. Kathmandu Print Shop says its pricing depends on paper type, printing method, finishing and quantity.

Quantity, boxes and extras

Quantity cuts both ways. A bigger order usually lowers the price of each card, but the total bill grows. Many families also need more than one card. The same Kathmandu Post feature quoted a card designer who said a single client often orders cards for five different ceremonies.

Then come the extras that are easy to forget:

- Boxes or envelopes, and sweets or dry fruit packed with the card
- Extra prints when the guest list grows late
- A reprint if a name, date or time is wrong
- Separate cards for the reception or bhoj

The hidden cost: distribution

The cost that rarely appears on a quote is handing the cards out. In the Kathmandu Valley, that can mean many evenings of driving or riding across the city, plus fuel, plus time away from work. Some families send younger relatives with stacks of cards for a whole week.

For relatives abroad, posting a card is slow and courier fees add up quickly. Many families end up sending those relatives a photo of the card on WhatsApp, which is already a digital invitation in all but name.

When you ask for a quote, give every printer the same details: paper, size, number of pages, finish, box or envelope, and quantity. Ask how many days the print run takes and what a reprint costs. Chandragiri Digital Print suggests ordering two to three months before the wedding.

What a Digital Wedding Card in Nepal Costs

A digital invitation has a different cost shape. You pay for the design and setup once. After that, sending it to 50 guests or 800 guests costs the same.

At Nimtto, for example, the prices on the pricing page are fixed and paid once, with no subscription and no charge per guest:

- Standard, Rs 2,999: a ready-made design with names, date, venue, RSVP and a WhatsApp link
- Pro, Rs 4,999: adds photos and your story, every ceremony with maps, music and the opening scene
- Pro Max, Rs 6,999: adds premium designs, personal guest links and priority help until the wedding
- Custom, from Rs 11,111: a design made for your occasion

Other digital options exist too, from free templates to video cards. The cheapest ones are often a single image, which works but cannot show every event, collect replies or be updated later. Compare what you get, not only the price.

Wedding Card Etiquette in Nepal: What Elders Expect

This is the part that worries most families, and for good reason. Wedding card etiquette in Nepal has always been about respect as much as information.

Handing over a card in person is a sign of respect. The Bihebazaar guide notes that people still want to distribute cards the traditional way because it seems respectful to guests and is part of the culture. The Kathmandu Post put it simply: social media brought the e-vite, but many in Kathmandu still prefer the traditional invite.

In practice, many families follow a few common patterns:

- Senior relatives (grandparents, elder uncles and aunts, the family's older generation) often expect a visit or at least a phone call.
- Close family usually hears the news in person or by phone long before any card arrives.
- Friends, colleagues and neighbours are generally comfortable with a WhatsApp or Viber invitation, especially younger guests.
- Relatives abroad cannot receive a card by hand anyway, so a digital invitation is often the most practical way to include them properly.

Customs vary by family, community and region. A family in Kathmandu may feel very different from a family in a smaller town. If you are unsure, ask the eldest person in your family how they would like each household to be invited.

A link alone is rarely enough for elders. What makes a digital invitation feel respectful is the personal step around it: a call, a voice note, or a visit with a small number of printed cards.

What Families Prefer (and Why It Varies)

There is no reliable survey of Nepali families on this question, so be wary of anyone who quotes a percentage. What we can describe are patterns that come up again and again when families plan.

Families with many relatives abroad tend to lean digital. A link reaches Sydney, Doha and Texas on the same day, and those guests can see every event, the venue map and the dates in one place.

Families with very senior relatives, or close ties to a village or a traditional community, tend to keep printed cards for those households. The card is part of the visit, and the visit is the real invitation.

Younger couples who plan their own wedding often push for digital to save time. Their parents may want printed cards. The mixed approach usually settles this kindly, because both sides get what matters to them.

Cards have also grown more elaborate over the years. As far back as 2005, a Nepali Times columnist wrote about invitations getting gaudier and bigger, with several cards for different parties of the same couple. For some families, a digital invitation is a relief from that race.

The Mixed Approach: A Small Print Run Plus a Link

This is the plan many families settle on, and it works well.

1. Make the digital invitation first. Put in every ceremony, time, venue and map. Check the names and dates with the designer before anyone sees it.
2. List the households who need a card in hand. Grandparents, senior relatives, family gurus, and anyone without a smartphone.
3. Print a small, good run for that list. Since you need fewer cards, you can choose better paper or a nicer finish for the same budget.
4. Add a QR code or short link on the printed card. Elders' children and grandchildren can open it for the map and the full programme.
5. Send the link to everyone else with a personal message, and call the people who matter most.

The printed card does the respectful work. The digital one does the practical work: maps, timings, replies and last-minute changes.

A golden palace gate opening on a phone screen, from the Mahal digital wedding invitation design

How to Send an Online Wedding Invitation in Nepal Respectfully

An online wedding invitation in Nepal is judged by how you send it. A few habits make all the difference.

- Send it to each person or household, not to a big group.
- Use their name and the relation you call them by (Thulobuwa, Maiju, Didi).
- Write one or two lines in your own words.
- Call elders before or after you send the link.
- Ask relatives who are close to an elder to help them open it.

If you need full invitation text, our guide to wedding invitation wording in Nepali and English has formal and family versions. The messages below are what you send with the link.

WhatsApp message for elders (Nepali):
आदरणीय [नाम] हजुर,
नमस्कार। हाम्रो [छोरा/छोरी] [नाम] को शुभ विवाह [मिति] मा [स्थान] मा हुँदैछ।
यस शुभ अवसरमा हजुरको उपस्थिति र आशीर्वादको हामी हार्दिक अपेक्षा गर्दछौं।
सबै कार्यक्रमको समय र नक्सा यो लिङ्कमा छ: [link]
म चाँडै हजुरलाई फोन पनि गर्नेछु।
[तपाईंको नाम] र परिवार

WhatsApp message for friends:
Hi [Name]! We are getting married on [date] at [venue] and we would love to have you there.
All the events, times and maps are here: [link]
Please tap RSVP by [date] so we can plan food and seating.
See you soon,
[Your names]

Phone call to an elder:
Namaste [Thulobuwa / Maiju / title], ma [your name] boldai chhu.
[Name] ko bibaha [date] ma pakka bhayo, hajurlai nimto dina phone gareko.
Hajur aaunu bhayo bhane hamilai thulo aashirbad hunchha.
Sabai bibaran hajurko phone ma pathaidinchhu, ra [day] ma card liyera aaunchhu.

(In English: Namaste, this is [your name]. [Name]'s wedding is fixed for [date], and I am calling to invite you. Your presence would be a great blessing for us. I will send all the details to your phone, and I will bring the card on [day].)

Message for relatives abroad:
Dear [Name],
[Bride's name] and [Groom's name] are getting married in [city] on [date in BS] ([date in AD]).
We know travelling home is not easy, but you are in our hearts for this day.
The full programme, venue maps and photos are here: [link]
If you can come, please RSVP by [date]. If not, we will feel your blessings from afar.
With love,
[Your names] and family

Note for the printed card (beside the QR code):
सबै कार्यक्रमको समय, स्थान र नक्साका लागि यो QR कोड स्क्यान गर्नुहोस्।
Scan for every ceremony, venue map and RSVP.
[short link]

For families with many guests overseas, our guide to inviting relatives abroad to a Nepali wedding covers timing and time zones in more detail. The families abroad page explains how Nimtto works when the couple or the family lives overseas.

On a Pro Max invitation, each guest can get a personal link with their own name on it. That small touch helps a digital card feel addressed to one person, the way a handed-over card does.

Mistakes to Avoid With Either Option

Most invitation problems come from rushing. These are the ones families mention most often.

- Forwarding one image to a big group. It feels careless, and people may miss it in a busy chat.
- Forgetting the BS and AD dates. Many elders think in Bikram Sambat. Show both.
- Skipping the call to elders. A link without a call can feel cold to the older generation.
- Printing before the details are final. A wrong time on 300 cards is an expensive mistake. Finalise the digital version first, then print.
- Leaving out maps. Guests from outside the city, and drivers, need a clear venue pin for each event.
- No RSVP date. Without one, you will be counting guests by phone in the last week.

Choosing What Fits Your Family

Start with your guest list, not with the card. Mark the households who need a visit, the ones who need a call, and the ones who will be happy with a message. That list tells you how many cards to print and who gets a link.

If you choose to go digital for most guests, take a look at the Nimtto designs for Nepali weddings, such as the Kham envelope with its red wax seal or the golden Patan door of Dhoka. The wedding invitation card online page shows what a full invitation includes, and the pricing page lists every plan.

### Is it rude to send a wedding invitation on WhatsApp in Nepal?
Not if you make it personal. Write the guest's name, add a warm line in your own words, and call your elders as well. What feels rude is a forwarded link with no greeting, sent to a big group.

### How many printed cards should we order if we also send a digital invitation?
Count the households who truly need a card in hand: grandparents, senior relatives, family priests or gurus, and anyone who does not use a smartphone. Add a few spares for people you forgot. Many families find this is a small share of the full guest list.

### How early should we send a digital wedding card in Nepal?
Send it about the same time you would hand out cards, usually a few weeks before the first ceremony. Relatives abroad need more notice, so tell them the date as soon as it is fixed, then send the full invitation later.

### Can a digital invitation show the date in Bikram Sambat?
Yes. A good Nepali digital invitation shows the date in BS and AD together. Nimtto invitations on the Nepal site do this, and the text can be in Nepali, English or both. See the [features](/features/) page.

### Can we change the venue or time after sending a digital invitation?
Yes, and this is one of its biggest advantages. You update the invitation and the same link shows the new details. Still send a short message to guests so they notice the change.

### Do guests need to download an app to open an online wedding invitation?
Not with Nimtto. Guests tap one link in WhatsApp, Viber, email or SMS and it opens in their phone's browser. There is no account to make. Read [how it works](/how-it-works/).

### Is a printed card still worth it as a keepsake?
For many families, yes. A printed card can sit in a photo album for decades. If keepsake value matters to you, print a small number of good cards for close family rather than a large number of cheap ones.

## How to Invite Relatives Abroad to a Wedding in Nepal
URL: https://nimtto.com/blog/invite-relatives-abroad-nepal-wedding/
By Nimtto Team · Published 2026-10-18 · Updated 2026-10-18
A practical guide for families in Nepal with relatives in the USA, UK, Australia, the Gulf and beyond: when to tell them, how to write dates and times, and what to send.

To invite relatives abroad to a wedding in Nepal, tell them early, by phone, as soon as the sait is fixed. Follow with a save the date, then the full invitation with each event's date in both BS and AD, the time marked as Nepal Time, the venue and a way to RSVP. Send it where they already talk to you: WhatsApp, Viber, Messenger or email.

The rest of this guide explains each step: how much notice to give, a time zone table for common countries, visa basics for relatives with foreign passports, posting cards to elders, and copy-ready messages you can send today. If most of your family lives overseas, the Nepali families abroad page shows how one invitation link can reach everyone at once.

How Early to Invite Relatives Abroad to a Wedding in Nepal

Relatives overseas need far more notice than guests in Kathmandu. They have to ask for leave, book long flights and sometimes arrange visas or school holidays for children. Flights home also tend to fill up in the busy months.

Nepal's main wedding season adds pressure. The Kathmandu Post describes Mangsir, Magh and Falgun, roughly December to February, as the country's main wedding season. Onlinekhabar explains why so many weddings crowd into a few auspicious dates, which also means venues, flights and family schedules fill up together.

A simple timeline

| When | What to send | Who |
|---|---|---|
| The day the sait is fixed | A phone or video call | Parents, grandparents, close relatives abroad |
| Within a week or two | A save the date message | Everyone abroad you plan to invite |
| Once venues and times are final | The full invitation with RSVP | All guests |
| About two weeks before | A reminder with times and travel notes | Guests who said yes |
| A few days before | A final reminder and video call details | Everyone, including those not coming |
| After the wedding | A thank-you message with a photo | All guests and well-wishers |

For a sense of how much notice travelling guests expect, The Knot's save the date guide says save the dates should go out no later than six months before the wedding, and that under four months is too late. Nepali families often get the sait closer to the date than that, which is exactly why the first phone call matters.

If the sait is still being fixed, tell relatives the likely month anyway. "We are planning a wedding in Mangsir, exact date coming soon" lets them start asking for leave.

Save the Date First, Then the Invitation

A save the date is a short note that says who is getting married, when and where. It does not need times, a venue or every event yet. For a Nepali wedding for relatives abroad, it is the most useful message you will send, because it starts their planning months earlier.

The full invitation follows once the details are fixed. This is where you list each ceremony, such as mehendi, janti, the wedding and the reception bhoj, with its own date, time and venue. If you need help with formal lines, the wedding invitation wording guide has Nepali and English examples you can adapt.

Time Zones: Nepal Time Versus Where Your Relatives Live

Nepal runs on Nepal Time (NPT), which is UTC+5:45, and timeanddate.com notes that Nepal does not use daylight saving time. The 45 minutes catches many people out, so always write the Nepal time clearly and, for live calls, the local time too.

The table uses the winter wedding season (Mangsir to Falgun). It shows the difference from Nepal and what 7:00 pm in Kathmandu means for each place.

| Where relatives live | Clock during the wedding season | Difference from Nepal | 7:00 pm in Kathmandu is |
|---|---|---|---|
| New York, Toronto (Eastern) | UTC-5 | 10 h 45 min behind | 8:15 am, same day |
| California, Vancouver (Pacific) | UTC-8 | 13 h 45 min behind | 5:15 am, same day |
| London, UK | UTC+0 | 5 h 45 min behind | 1:15 pm, same day |
| Sydney, Melbourne | UTC+11 (summer time) | 5 h 15 min ahead | 12:15 am, next day |
| Dubai, Abu Dhabi | UTC+4 | 1 h 45 min behind | 5:15 pm, same day |
| Doha, Riyadh, Kuwait | UTC+3 | 2 h 45 min behind | 4:15 pm, same day |
| Tokyo, Seoul | UTC+9 | 3 h 15 min ahead | 10:15 pm, same day |

Watch for daylight saving changes

Because Nepal never changes its clocks, the gap moves when other countries do. The USA, Canada, the UK and parts of Australia switch between summer and winter time, and the timeanddate.com daylight saving guide lists the exact dates each year. For example, the gap to New York is 10 h 45 min in winter but 9 h 45 min in summer. Gulf countries and Japan do not change their clocks, so their gap stays the same all year.

An evening event in Kathmandu can fall after midnight in Australia. If relatives there plan to watch on a video call, write their local date as well as the time.

Write the Date in Both BS and AD

Your elders think in Bikram Sambat. Your cousin in Texas thinks in AD. A date written only one way leads to calls, guesswork and, sometimes, a booked flight on the wrong day.

Write both, with the day of the week, for every event:

- Good: Shukrabar, [gate] Mangsir 2083 BS ([date] [month] 2026 AD), 11:00 am Nepal Time
- Risky: [gate] Mangsir, 11 am

Check every conversion against a trusted Nepali calendar before you send anything. If a ceremony starts at night, such as a late lagan, give the AD date carefully, because the event may run past midnight.

Visas for Relatives With Foreign Passports

Many relatives abroad now hold another country's passport. They will need to sort out entry before they fly. Keep your advice general and point them to the official sources, because rules, fees and lists of eligible countries can change.

The Department of Immigration is the official source for Nepal visas. Many foreign passport holders can get a tourist visa on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, and the department offers an online form that can be filled in before travel. Citizens of some countries cannot get a visa on arrival and must apply through a Nepali embassy first.

Relatives of Nepali origin

Relatives who were born Nepali, or whose parents or grandparents were, may qualify for a Non-Resident Nepali (NRN) identity card. The Embassy of Nepal in Washington explains that foreign nationals of Nepali origin with this card still need a visa, but it is issued free of charge at entry points. Ask them to check the current rules with their nearest Nepali embassy well before the wedding.

Do not give relatives exact visa fees or rules from memory. Send them the official link and let them confirm for their own passport.

How to Send the Invitation Abroad

Choose the channel your relatives already use. One family group can hold relatives on four continents, but elders often prefer a personal message or a paper card.

Messaging apps and email

WhatsApp, Viber and Messenger reach relatives anywhere in moments, and they are free over the internet. Email works well for formal invitations to older relatives, in-laws and colleagues of the family. Whatever you use, send a personal line first and the invitation after, never only a forwarded picture.

To send a wedding invitation to the USA from Nepal, an online invitation link is the simplest route. It opens on any phone, needs no app, and you can update a time or venue later without sending a new card to everyone.

Postal cards for elders

Some grandparents and senior relatives abroad treasure a paper card. If you post one, send it early, because international mail can be slow and delivery times vary by country. For important cards, Nepal Post's EMS service is a time-bound express option. Send the digital invitation too, so they have the details even if the card is late. For the full trade-offs, see digital vs printed wedding cards in Nepal.

RSVP: Why Counts Matter for the Bhoj

Caterers and party venues in Nepal plan food by head count. Guests from abroad are hard to count, because plans can change with flights and leave. A clear RSVP with a reply date helps you avoid both waste and empty plates.

Ask three things: will they come, how many people, and which events. A relative flying in for one week may come to the wedding and the reception but miss the mehendi. With an online invitation, guests reply on the invitation itself, and Nimtto shows who is coming, how many and to which events in your dashboard, which you can export for the caterer. The features page explains how replies work.

Himal design showing a Himalayan sunrise and photo story on a phone

For Relatives Who Cannot Come

Some relatives will not manage the trip, and that is fine. Invite them anyway. Being invited tells them they are still part of the family, and many will send blessings, a gift or a video message.

Make it easy for them to join from afar. Share a video call link for the main ceremony, and tell them the start time in their own time zone. Ask a cousin to hold the phone near the mandap so elders abroad can see the rituals. Afterwards, send photos and a short thank-you note.

Nepali Wedding Invitation Wording for Relatives Abroad

These messages are ready to copy. Replace the words in square brackets and change the tone to suit each relative.

Save the date for relatives abroad:
Namaste [Name] ji,
We have happy news! [Groom's name] and [Bride's name] are getting married in Nepal.
Please save the date: [gate] Mangsir 2083 BS ([date] AD) in [City].
We know travel takes planning, so we wanted you to hear first.
The full invitation with all event times will follow.
With love, [Your names]

Invitation message for family overseas:
Namaste [Name] ji,
With great joy, we invite you and your family to the wedding of
[Groom's name] and [Bride's name].
Wedding: [Day], [gate] [month] 2083 BS ([date] AD), [time] Nepal Time
Reception bhoj: [Day], [date] AD, from [time] Nepal Time
Venue: [Venue name], [City]
All events, maps and RSVP are here: [link]
Please reply by [date] so we can plan the bhoj.

Reminder for guests travelling from abroad:
Hello [Name] ji, we are so happy you are coming!
A quick reminder for your trip:
Wedding on [date] AD at [time] Nepal Time, [venue].
Nepal Time is UTC+5:45, so it is [local time] in [their city].
Call [contact name] on [phone number] when you land.
Safe travels, see you soon!

Message to elders abroad (Nepali):
आदरणीय [नाम] ज्यू,
सादर नमस्कार। हाम्रो छोरा/छोरी [नाम] को विवाह
मिति २०८३ [महिना] [गते] ([AD date]) मा [सहर] मा हुने भएको छ।
हजुरको आशीर्वाद हाम्रा लागि सबैभन्दा ठूलो उपहार हो।
आउन मिल्ने भए सपरिवार पाल्नुहोला, नमिले भिडियो कलमा सँगै हुनुहोला।
निमन्त्रणा यहाँ छ: [link]

Thank-you message after the wedding:
Dear [Name] ji,
Thank you for your blessings and love for [Groom's name] and [Bride's name].
Having you with us, in [City] or on a video call from [their city],
it meant so much to the whole family.
Here are a few photos from the day: [link]
With love and gratitude, [Your names]

Final Thoughts

Inviting family overseas comes down to a few habits. Call early, write every date in BS and AD, mark times as Nepal Time, point visa questions to official sites, and ask for an RSVP by a clear date. Do those, and your relatives can plan with confidence.

Nimtto makes online wedding invitations with every ceremony, maps, BS and AD dates and RSVP, set up with a real designer. See the Nepali families abroad page for how it helps families split across countries. Designs like Himal, Durbar and Dhoka bring a touch of home to every screen, and plans are on the pricing page. If a cousin abroad is planning their own wedding overseas, point them to the international site.

### How early should we tell relatives abroad about a wedding in Nepal?
Tell them by phone the day the sait is fixed, then send a save the date soon after. Relatives who need leave from work and long-haul flights usually need several months of notice.

### Do relatives with a foreign passport need a visa to attend a wedding in Nepal?
Most foreign passport holders need a visa, and many can get a tourist visa on arrival. Rules and fees change, so ask them to check the [Department of Immigration](https://www.nepalimmigration.gov.np/) or the nearest Nepali embassy before booking.

### What time should we write on an invitation for guests abroad?
Write the Nepal time and add "Nepal Time (NPT)" after it. For a live video call, also list the time in the main cities where your relatives live, so nobody has to work it out.

### Is it fine to send a wedding invitation abroad on WhatsApp?
Yes. Most families abroad keep in touch on WhatsApp, Viber or Messenger. Call senior relatives first, then send the link, so the invitation feels personal.

### How do we send a wedding invitation to the USA from Nepal?
The fastest way is a digital invitation by message or email. If an elder would value a paper card, post it early or use an express service such as EMS, because international post can take a while.

### Should we invite relatives abroad even if they probably cannot come?
Yes. Being invited matters to family even when travel is not possible. Make it clear that their blessings are welcome and offer a video call on the day.

### Can relatives abroad RSVP online?
Yes. With an online invitation that has RSVP, they reply from their phone, choose which events they will attend and say how many are coming. Nimtto shows these replies in your [dashboard](/features/).

## Pasni (Annaprashan) Invitation Guide: Wording, Date and What to Include
URL: https://nimtto.com/blog/pasni-invitation-guide/
By Nimtto Team · Published 2026-10-18 · Updated 2026-10-18
Everything to put on a pasni (annaprashan) invitation, from the sait and the bhoj time to copy-ready wording in Nepali and English for cards, WhatsApp and reminders.

A good pasni invitation card tells guests four things clearly: whose pasni it is, the sait date (in both BS and AD), the time of the puja and the bhoj, and where to come. Add the parents' or grandparents' names as hosts, a contact number and a simple way to reply, and you have everything a guest needs.

This guide covers what pasni means, how the date is chosen, a checklist of what to include, and copy-ready pasni invitation wording in Nepali and English. You will also find a WhatsApp message, a reminder and practical tips for planning a celebration around a baby's naps.

What Is Pasni (Annaprashan)?

Pasni is the rice feeding ceremony in Nepal, the day a baby eats solid food for the first time. In Sanskrit it is called annaprashan, and Newar families know it as macha janku. Wikipedia's article on Annaprashana notes that this rite is still widely kept in Nepal, even as some other old rites have faded.

The day usually starts with a puja at home or at a temple, followed by the first taste of food and a family meal. In cities, it can be a small home gathering or a full party with a hall and a bhoj.

Usual age for boys and girls

The custom most families follow is simple. Tearfund's notes on weaning practices in Nepal describe the ceremony at five months for a girl and six months for a boy. A Nepali family blog from Australia gives the same pattern, adding that some families hold a girl's pasni in the seventh month.

| | Baby girl | Baby boy |
|---|---|---|
| Usual month | 5th (some families choose the 7th) | 6th |
| Who fixes the exact day | Family priest or astrologer | Family priest or astrologer |
| First food | Kheer (rice pudding) or rice | Kheer (rice pudding) or rice |

The first taste and the choosing game

The first food is usually a little kheer, given from a silver bowl or spoon. Who feeds it first differs from family to family. Wikipedia describes the mother feeding first in Nepal, while in other homes an elder starts and then everyone takes a turn. In one family's account of their daughter's pasni, the grandmother cooked the kheer and each relative fed a small spoonful.

Many families also play a choosing game. A tray is set in front of the baby with things like a book, a pen, jewellery, clay or soil, and food. Whatever the baby touches first is said, in fun, to hint at the child's future, and the same blog describes the whole room cheering at the choice.

Customs vary by community and family. Ask the elders on both sides how your family does it, then plan the invitation and timing around that.

How the Pasni Date Is Chosen

Most families do not pick the date themselves. A family priest or astrologer reads the baby's birth chart and gives a sait, an auspicious day and time. Wikipedia notes that in Nepal the date and time are chosen by an astrologer.

Ask for the sait early, ideally soon after the baby turns four months. That gives you time to book a venue, tell relatives outside the valley and send invitations. If the priest offers two or three good days, choose the one that suits the baby's routine and the most important guests.

Once you have the sait, write down two times: the puja time and the bhoj time. Guests often only need the bhoj time, but close family will want to be there for the puja and the first taste.

What to Include on a Pasni Invitation Card

A pasni card is shorter than a wedding card, but guests still need every practical detail. Use this checklist before you print or share anything.

| Item | What to write | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Child's name | The name the family uses | Add "our son" or "our daughter" so guests know |
| Hosts | Parents' names, or grandparents if they host | Name both parents together |
| Grandparents | Optional line, "with blessings from..." | Common when the elders are hosting |
| Date | BS and AD, plus the day of the week | Example: Shukrabar, [gate] [month] 2083 BS ([date] AD) |
| Time | Puja time and bhoj time separately | Say "onwards" for the bhoj |
| Venue | Full name, area, city | Add a map link on digital invitations |
| Bhoj | Lunch or dinner, and from what time | Helps guests plan their day |
| RSVP | Name and phone number, and a reply date | Ask how many people are coming |
| Small notes | Parking, dress, quiet timing for the baby | Keep it to one line |

Two small notes help a lot at a baby's event. First, ask guests to arrive on time for the puja, because a baby's good mood does not last forever. Second, if you would prefer no flash photography or strong perfume near the baby, say so kindly in one short line.

Write the date both ways. Elders read the Bikram Sambat date, while younger guests and relatives abroad often check the AD date in their phone calendar.

Pasni Card Matter in Nepali

Here is pasni card matter in Nepali that you can copy and change. Replace the words in square brackets with your own details. Use छोरा for a son and छोरी for a daughter.

Formal Nepali invitation from the parents:
सादर निमन्त्रणा

हाम्रो प्रिय छोरा/छोरी [बच्चाको नाम] को
पास्नी (अन्नप्राशन) संस्कार
मिति २०८३ [महिना] [गते], [बार]
([AD date]) का दिन शुभसाइतमा गर्ने भएकोले
उक्त शुभअवसरमा सपरिवार पाल्नुहुन
हार्दिक अनुरोध गर्दछौँ ।

पूजा: बिहान [समय]
भोज: दिउँसो [समय] देखि
स्थान: [ठाउँको नाम], [सहर]

निमन्त्रक
[बुबाको नाम] / [आमाको नाम]
सम्पर्क: [फोन नम्बर]

When grandparents host, the card usually names them first, with the parents mentioned under the child's name. Use नाति for a grandson and नातिनी for a granddaughter.

Nepali invitation from the grandparents:
सादर निमन्त्रणा

हाम्रो नाति/नातिनी [बच्चाको नाम]
(सुपुत्र/सुपुत्री: [बुबाको नाम] र [आमाको नाम]) को
पास्नी मिति २०८३ [महिना] [गते], [बार]
([AD date]) का दिन हुने भएकोले
यस खुसीको अवसरमा सपरिवार पाल्नुहुन
हार्दिक अनुरोध गर्दछौँ ।

भोज: [समय] देखि
स्थान: [ठाउँको नाम], [सहर]

निमन्त्रक
[हजुरबुबाको नाम] / [हजुरआमाको नाम]
सम्पर्क: [फोन नम्बर]

Pasni Invitation Wording in English

English wording works well for friends, colleagues and relatives who read English more easily. Keep it short and warm. A baby's pasni is a family celebration, so the tone can be softer than a wedding card.

Formal English invitation:
With joy and blessings
[Father's name] and [Mother's name]
invite you and your family to the
Pasni (Annaprashan) of our son/daughter
[Child's name]

[Day], [gate] [month] 2083 BS ([date] AD)
Puja at [time], lunch from [time] onwards
[Venue name], [Area], [City]

Kindly reply to [Name] on [phone number]

Warm and simple English invitation:
[Child's name] is ready for a first taste of rice!
Please join us for a small pasni and lunch.

[Day], [date] AD ([gate] [month] 2083 BS)
From [time]
[Venue or "at our home"], [Area]

Your blessings mean the world to us.
[Parents' names]

WhatsApp Message and Reminder for a Pasni

Most guests will see your invitation on their phone first. A short personal message with the link or card picture feels warmer than a forwarded image with no words. Call the most important elders before you send anything.

WhatsApp invitation message:
Namaste [Name] ji,
Our [son/daughter] [Child's name] has the pasni on
[Day], [gate] [month] 2083 BS ([date] AD).
Puja at [time], lunch from [time], at [venue].
We would love you and your family to come and bless [him/her].
Here is the invitation: [link]
Please let us know how many will come.

Reminder message (send 1 to 2 days before):
नमस्ते! [बच्चाको नाम] को पास्नी भोलि [बार] छ।
पूजा [समय] मा, भोज [समय] देखि, [स्थान] मा।
नक्सा: [map link]
हजुरहरूलाई पर्खिरहेका छौँ।

Namaste! A gentle reminder that [Child's name]'s pasni is tomorrow.
Puja at [time], lunch from [time], at [venue]. See you there!

Planning Around the Baby: Guests, Timing and Size

A pasni is the baby's day, but the baby has no idea about the schedule. Planning around the child's needs keeps the day happy for everyone.

Keep the guest list small enough

A crowded room is loud and warm, and babies tire quickly. Many families invite close relatives for the puja and a wider circle for the bhoj. If space is tight, it is fine to keep the pasni small and celebrate the first birthday with more people later.

Fit the times around naps and feeds

Ask the parents when the baby usually sleeps and feeds, and set the puja for a time the baby is normally awake and calm. Morning often works well. Leave a short gap between the puja and the bhoj so the mother can feed the baby and rest.

Make space for the mother and baby

Set aside a quiet room near the venue where the mother can feed, change or settle the baby. Tell close family where it is. Ask guests kindly to wash their hands before holding the baby, and keep the number of people passing the baby around small.

Give elders and far-away relatives notice

Grandparents and the mama's side usually expect a personal call, not only a message. Relatives in other cities need enough time to travel. For family abroad, a video call during the puja lets them watch the first taste live, even from the other side of the world.

Write the RSVP date on the invitation. Even a small bhoj needs a head count for food, and replies are much easier to collect when guests know the deadline.

Online or Printed: Choosing the Right Pasni Card

Some families still print a small number of cards for elders, and that is a lovely touch. For most guests, though, an online pasni invitation is easier. It reaches relatives in Pokhara, Dubai or Sydney at the same moment, and nobody has to deliver cards door to door with a newborn at home.

With Nimtto, a designer sets up your pasni invitation as a short animated card that opens on the guest's phone, with the date in BS and AD, the venue and a Google Maps link, and RSVP. You can see how it works on the pasni invitation page and the how it works page. Replies go to your dashboard, so you can see who is coming and how many without counting messages one by one.

Sayapatri design with marigold strings in a doorway, shown on a phone

Soft, family-like designs suit a baby's day. Sayapatri has marigold strings in a doorway, Gurans opens through a gate of roses and marigold, and Laali is blush pink and gold with lanterns. You can browse every option on the designs page.

Pasni, Nwaran and Other Family Ceremonies

Pasni is one of several family ceremonies in a child's early life. The first is usually nwaran, the naming ceremony, which Wikipedia describes as commonly held on the eleventh day after birth. If you are planning both, you can keep the same design style for a matching set, and the nwaran invitation page shows how that looks.

Later milestones follow the same pattern: a clear date, a sait, a family meal and a guest list. When your son reaches the age for bratabandha, the bratabandha invitation guide covers the wording and planning. For a bigger family wedding, the wedding invitation wording guide has formal Nepali and English examples.

Final Thoughts

A pasni invitation does not need to be long. It needs the child's name, the sait in BS and AD, clear puja and bhoj times, the venue and an easy way to reply. Write it with warmth, call the elders first, and plan the day around the baby rather than the clock.

If you would like an online pasni invitation that family near and far can open with one link, look through the designs and compare plans on the pricing page. Nimtto's Standard plan (Rs 2,999) covers a ready-made design with names, date, venue and RSVP, which is often all a pasni needs.

### At what age is pasni done for a baby girl and a baby boy?
It is commonly held in the fifth month for a girl and the sixth month for a boy, though some families choose the seventh month for a girl. The final day comes from the sait your family priest or astrologer gives.

### Who is invited to a pasni?
Close family always comes, especially both sets of grandparents and the baby's maternal uncle (mama) and aunts. Many families also invite neighbours and close friends for the bhoj, but a small guest list is easier on the baby.

### Should a pasni invitation say the baby's full name?
Use the name the family will call the child. Many children also receive a name from their birth chart at nwaran, and some families prefer to keep that one private, so write whichever name you are happy to share.

### How early should we send pasni invitations?
Send them as soon as the sait is fixed. Two to three weeks is comfortable for local guests, and relatives in other cities or abroad should hear the date by phone first, even before the card is ready.

### Is it rude to send a pasni invitation on WhatsApp?
No. Most families now share invitations on WhatsApp or Viber. A short personal call to elders and the mama's side, followed by the link, keeps it respectful.

### What gift should guests bring to a pasni?
Common gifts are clothes, a small silver or gold item, toys, or cash in an envelope with your blessing. The invitation does not need to mention gifts unless you want to say blessings are enough.

### Can we hold the pasni at a hotel or party venue?
Yes. Many families keep the puja at home in the morning and hold the bhoj at a hall or restaurant later. If you do this, list both places and times clearly on the card.

### Can Nimtto make an online pasni invitation in Nepali?
Yes. Nimtto makes animated pasni invitations in English and Nepali, with dates in BS and AD, a map link and RSVP. See the [pasni invitation page](/occasions/pasni/) or [pricing](/pricing/).

## Wedding Invitation Wording in Nepali and English (Copy-Ready Examples)
URL: https://nimtto.com/blog/wedding-invitation-wording-nepali-english/
By Nimtto Team · Published 2026-10-18 · Updated 2026-10-18
Copy-ready Nepali and English wording for a wedding card, from the invocation line to the RSVP, plus short messages to send with your invitation link.

The usual wedding invitation wording in Nepali follows a fixed order: an invocation such as ॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥, the heading शुभ विवाह, the parents' names, the couple's names, the ceremony dates in Bikram Sambat, the venue, and a closing line from the family (दर्शनाभिलाषी or निवेदक, followed by सपरिवार). Keep the honorifics the same from start to finish and write the BS date first, with AD in brackets.

Below you will find a table of that structure and more than a dozen copy-ready blocks: formal Nepali from the bride's side and the groom's side, English and bilingual versions, a bhoj-only card, RSVP and blessings lines, and short WhatsApp messages. Change the names in square brackets and they are ready to use.

How a Nepali wedding card is structured

Most Nepali wedding card matter, printed or online, moves from the sacred to the practical. The invocation and heading come first, then the families, then the plans, then the people who invite you. If you keep that order, elders will find the card proper and younger guests will find what they need.

| Part | Nepali term | What goes in it | Tip |
|---|---|---|---|
| Invocation | मङ्गलाचरण | ॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥ or a short verse your family uses | Ask elders which line your family prefers |
| Heading | शुभ विवाह | The words "Shubha Bibaha" (auspicious wedding) | Often in a larger, decorative script |
| Hosts | आमाबुबा | The parents who send the card | Use श्रीमान् and श्रीमती consistently |
| The couple | सुपुत्र / सुपुत्री | Groom and bride, each with their parents' names | Spell names the way the couple writes them |
| Ceremonies | कार्यक्रम | Each rite with date, time and venue | One line per event is easiest to read |
| Feast | प्रीतिभोज / स्वागत समारोह | Dinner or reception time and place | Say "onwards" if there is no end time |
| Request | अनुरोध | The polite request to attend and bless the couple | सपरिवार invites the whole household |
| Signature | दर्शनाभिलाषी / निवेदक | Grandparents, parents, siblings, "and family" | Seniors first |
| RSVP and contact | सम्पर्क | One or two phone numbers, a reply date | A named person, not just a number |

On an online invitation the same order still works. The difference is that each ceremony can carry its own map link, and guests reply on the page instead of calling you.

Formal wedding invitation wording in Nepali

These blocks use हजुर and honorific verbs (उपस्थित भई, दिनुहुन) all the way through. That is the safest tone for a card that goes to grandparents, teachers and family elders. If your family normally writes तपाईं, change every instance, not only the first.

From the bride's family (कन्या पक्ष)

Formal Nepali card from the bride's parents:
॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥

शुभ विवाह

श्रीमान् [बुबाको नाम] तथा श्रीमती [आमाको नाम]की सुपुत्री
[दुलहीको नाम]
र
श्रीमान् [दुलहाका बुबाको नाम] तथा श्रीमती [दुलहाकी आमाको नाम]का सुपुत्र
चि. [दुलहाको नाम]

को शुभ विवाह मिति २०८३ साल फागुन १२ गते बुधबार हुने भएकाले उक्त शुभ अवसरमा हजुर सपरिवार उपस्थित भई नवदम्पतीलाई शुभ आशीर्वाद दिनुहुन हार्दिक अनुरोध गर्दछौं।

कार्यक्रम
जन्ती स्वागत: बेलुका ४:०० बजे
विवाह संस्कार: बेलुका ५:०० बजे
प्रीतिभोज: बेलुका ७:०० बजेदेखि

स्थान: [भेन्यूको नाम], [ठेगाना]

दर्शनाभिलाषी
[हजुरबुबा तथा हजुरआमाको नाम]
[बुबा तथा आमाको नाम] सपरिवार
सम्पर्क: [फोन नम्बर]

From the groom's family: the janti invitation (वर पक्ष)

The groom's side invites guests to walk with the janti (the wedding party) to the bride's home or venue. Say clearly where the janti leaves from and at what time, because that is the detail people forget.

Formal Nepali janti invitation from the groom's parents:
॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥

शुभ विवाह

हाम्रा सुपुत्र चि. [दुलहाको नाम]
र
श्रीमान् [दुलहीका बुबाको नाम] तथा श्रीमती [दुलहीकी आमाको नाम]की सुपुत्री
[दुलहीको नाम]

को शुभ विवाह मिति २०८३ साल फागुन १२ गते बुधबार हुने भएकाले सोही दिन दिउँसो २:०० बजे [घरको ठेगाना]बाट प्रस्थान हुने जन्तीमा सामेल भई तथा बेलुका ७:०० बजेदेखि हुने प्रीतिभोजमा सपरिवार उपस्थित भई नवदम्पतीलाई आशीर्वाद दिनुहुन हार्दिक अनुरोध गर्दछौं।

जन्ती प्रस्थान: [घरको ठेगाना], दिउँसो २:०० बजे
विवाह स्थल: [भेन्यूको नाम], [ठेगाना]

निवेदक
[बुबा तथा आमाको नाम] सपरिवार
सम्पर्क: [फोन नम्बर]

A shorter, warmer Nepali version

Some families want a simple biha ko nimto for friends and colleagues, without the full formal frame. This one is still polite but reads like a personal note.

Short Nepali wedding invitation for friends:
शुभ विवाह

हाम्रो छोरी [दुलहीको नाम] र [दुलहाको नाम]को विवाह २०८३ फागुन १२ गते बुधबार हुँदै छ।

यो खुसीको दिनमा हजुरको उपस्थिति र आशीर्वाद पाउँदा हामीलाई निकै खुसी लाग्नेछ।

स्थान: [भेन्यूको नाम], [ठेगाना]
प्रीतिभोज: बेलुका ७:०० बजेदेखि

[बुबा तथा आमाको नाम] परिवार

Before printing or sending, ask one elder to read the Nepali aloud. Spelling slips in names, and mixed honorifics such as हजुर in one line and तिमी in another, are easy to hear and hard to spot on a screen.

Wedding card wording in English for Nepal

English cards in Nepal tend to follow the South Asian style: the parents host, the programme is listed, and the card ends with "With best compliments from" and the family. That differs a little from American etiquette, where the hosts' line opens the card and gifts are never mentioned.

In American etiquette, Emily Post's guide to formal invitations keeps "the honour of your presence" for a ceremony in a house of worship and "the pleasure of your company" for other venues. On a Nepali card in English, either reads well, so choose the one your family likes.

Formal English card from the bride's parents:
Shubha Bibaha

Mr [Father's name] and Mrs [Mother's name] [Surname]
request the honour of your presence with family
at the wedding of their daughter
[Bride's name]
with
[Groom's name]
son of Mr [Father's name] and Mrs [Mother's name] [Surname]

Wednesday, 24 February 2027
(Falgun 12, 2083 B.S.)

Programme
Welcoming the janti: 4:00 pm
Wedding rites: 5:00 pm
Dinner: 7:00 pm onwards

Venue: [Venue name], [Address]

With best compliments from
[Grandparents' names] and family
Contact: [Phone number]

English janti invitation from the groom's family:
Shubha Bibaha

Mr and Mrs [Groom's parents' names]
warmly invite you and your family
to join the janti for the wedding of their son
[Groom's name]
with
[Bride's name]
daughter of Mr and Mrs [Bride's parents' names]

Wednesday, 24 February 2027 (Falgun 12, 2083 B.S.)

Janti departs: 2:00 pm from [Home address]
Wedding venue: [Venue name], [Address]
Dinner: 7:00 pm onwards

With love from
[Parents' names] and family

Modern English card from the couple and families:
Together with our families
[Bride's name] and [Groom's name]
invite you to celebrate our wedding

Wednesday, 24 February 2027
Falgun 12, 2083 B.S.
[Venue name], [City]

Wedding rites at 5:00 pm, dinner from 7:00 pm.
Your blessings mean the world to us.

Bilingual shubha bibaha invitation wording

A bilingual card helps when one side of the family reads Nepali and the other, or relatives abroad, read English more easily. Put each Nepali line directly above its English line so readers never lose their place.

Bilingual Nepali and English wedding card:
॥ श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥
शुभ विवाह | Shubha Bibaha

[बुबा तथा आमाको नाम]की सुपुत्री [दुलहीको नाम]
[Bride's name], daughter of [Parents' names]
र | with
[बुबा तथा आमाको नाम]का सुपुत्र चि. [दुलहाको नाम]
[Groom's name], son of [Parents' names]

२०८३ साल फागुन १२ गते बुधबार
Wednesday, 24 February 2027

हजुर सपरिवार उपस्थित भई नवदम्पतीलाई आशीर्वाद दिनुहुन हार्दिक अनुरोध गर्दछौं।
We warmly invite you and your family to bless the couple.

स्थान | Venue: [Venue name], [Address]
दर्शनाभिलाषी | With best compliments: [Family name] परिवार | family

On paper, two languages take double the space. Online, you can skip that trade-off: Nimtto invitations show Nepali and English versions of the same page, and each guest taps the language they prefer.

Writing the date in Bikram Sambat and AD

Bikram Sambat is Nepal's official calendar, and its year runs about 56 or 57 years ahead of AD depending on the month, as the Vikram Samvat entry on Wikipedia explains. Always fix the date with your priest's patro first, then convert it.

Wedding dates (sait) are worked out from the panchanga, and only some days in a season suit a wedding. Onlinekhabar's report on the wedding season explains that astrologers and the Nepal Panchanga Nirnayak Samiti set these days, which is why venues book out fast. Print the date only after the venue confirms.

Date line in Nepali (BS with AD):
मिति: वि.सं. २०८३ साल फागुन १२ गते, बुधबार
(तदनुसार सन् २०२७ फेब्रुअरी २४)

Date line in English (AD with BS):
Wednesday, 24 February 2027
(Falgun 12, 2083 B.S.)

A wedding rite that runs past midnight may fall on the next AD date while the family still calls it one BS day. Write the date your priest gives, and check the AD conversion twice.

Reception and bhoj only

Many families send a separate card for the reception or bhoj, often to office colleagues and neighbours who will not attend the rites. Keep it short, and say "onwards" when guests can come at any time in the evening. Our reception and bhoj page shows how an online version looks.

Nepali bhoj invitation:
हाम्रा सुपुत्र चि. [दुलहाको नाम] र बुहारी [दुलहीको नाम]को शुभ विवाहको उपलक्ष्यमा मिति २०८३ फागुन १४ गते शुक्रबार बेलुका ६:०० बजेदेखि [भेन्यूको नाम]मा आयोजना गरिएको प्रीतिभोजमा हजुर सपरिवार उपस्थित भइदिनुहुन हार्दिक अनुरोध गर्दछौं।

निवेदक
[बुबा तथा आमाको नाम] सपरिवार

English reception invitation:
Mr and Mrs [Parents' names]
invite you and your family to a reception
to celebrate the wedding of
[Groom's name] and [Bride's name]

Friday, 26 February 2027 (Falgun 14, 2083 B.S.)
6:00 pm onwards
[Venue name], [Address]

RSVP and blessings lines

An RSVP line is newer on Nepali cards, but it saves the caterer guessing. Give one date and one way to reply.

RSVP line in Nepali and English:
कृपया [मिति]भित्र आउने वा नआउने जानकारी गराइदिनुहुन अनुरोध छ।
Kindly let us know by [date] if you can join us.

Gifts are trickier. Emily Post advises leaving gifts off the invitation entirely, even "no gifts, please". The Knot suggests putting gift notes on the wedding website instead. If you still want to say it, keep it to one gentle line about blessings, in a notes section rather than on the front of the card.

Blessings instead of gifts:
हजुरको उपस्थिति र आशीर्वाद नै हाम्रा लागि सबैभन्दा ठूलो उपहार हो।
Your presence and blessings are the only gift we wish for.

WhatsApp messages to send with your invitation link

A link arrives better with a short personal note. Use the guest's name, say who is getting married, and tell them where to reply.

WhatsApp message in Nepali:
नमस्ते [नाम] ज्यू,
हाम्रो छोरी [दुलहीको नाम]को शुभ विवाहको निम्तो यस लिंकमा पठाएका छौं: [लिंक]
कार्यक्रम, समय र नक्सा सबै लिंकमै छन्। कृपया लिंकमै आउने जानकारी दिनुहोला।
[नाम] परिवार

WhatsApp message in English:
Namaste [Name],
We would love you to join us for [Bride's name] and [Groom's name]'s wedding. Our invitation is here: [link]
Every ceremony, time and map is on the page. Please reply on the invitation by [date].
With love, [Name] family

For relatives in other time zones, add the local time or ask them to check the date twice. Our guide to inviting relatives abroad to a Nepal wedding covers that in detail, and the families abroad page shows how they can reply from anywhere.

Mistakes to check before you send

A quick read for these slips will save reprints and awkward calls.

- Mixed honorifics. हजुर in the request and तपाईं in the RSVP line sounds careless. Pick one.
- Names that do not match. Spell each parent's name the way they sign it, in both scripts.
- Missing janti time. The groom's side must say where and when the janti leaves.
- Only one calendar. Older relatives look for BS, younger ones and guests abroad look for AD. Give both.
- No contact person. Write a name next to the phone number.
- Too many ceremonies on one card. If you also host a maagni or mehendi, list it separately or link to an engagement invitation.

If you are still deciding between paper and a link, our comparison of digital and printed wedding cards in Nepal lays out the costs and the trade-offs.

Putting your wording on an invitation

Once your wedding invitation wording in Nepali and English is ready, you can print it, send it as an image, or put it on an online invitation. The Kham design opens like an envelope with a red wax seal, Nimantrana unfolds as a red and gold card, and Mala uses red silk, marigolds and a kalash.

Phone screen showing the Kham wedding invitation, an envelope sealed with red wax

With Nimtto, a designer sets up your wording in Nepali and English, lists every ceremony with a map, and collects RSVPs in one place. Browse the wedding invitation designs, see how it works, or compare plans on the pricing page when you are ready.

### Who should be named as the host on a Nepali wedding card?
Usually the parents of the bride or groom, since they send the invitation. Many families also add the grandparents or the head of the household at the bottom, followed by सपरिवार (and family).

### What does सपरिवार mean on a wedding card?
It means "with your family". When you write सपरिवार उपस्थित भई, you are inviting the guest and their household, so leave it out if you can only host the person named.

### Should the date be written in Bikram Sambat or AD?
In Nepal, write the Bikram Sambat date first because that is what the priest and most relatives use. Add the AD date in brackets for younger guests and relatives abroad.

### Is it rude to send a wedding invitation on WhatsApp in Nepal?
Not if you send it personally, with the guest's name and a warm line. For grandparents and very senior relatives, a phone call or a visit after the message is still a kind touch.

### What is the difference between a bride's side card and a groom's side card?
The bride's family invites guests to welcome the janti and attend the wedding rites. The groom's family invites guests to join the janti procession and often a reception later.

### Can the couple invite guests in their own names?
Yes. Many couples now write "Together with our families" in English, or name both sets of parents. Formal Nepali cards still usually come from the parents.

### Can I use these wordings on an online invitation?
Yes. Paste them as they are or edit them. On a [Nimtto invitation](/features/) the Nepali and English versions sit on the same page and guests switch between them.

## Digital Wedding Invitation Etiquette: Is It OK to Send Wedding Invitations Online?
URL: https://nimtto.com/international/blog/digital-wedding-invitation-etiquette/
By Nimtto Team · Published 2026-10-18 · Updated 2026-10-18
Yes, for most weddings. Here is what etiquette experts say, when to add paper for some guests, and the exact wording to send with your link.

Is it OK to send wedding invitations online? Yes, for most weddings it is. Etiquette experts now treat digital invitations as acceptable, as long as they feel personal and match the formality of your day.

The best guide is a simple test from the Emily Post Institute: if you would be comfortable extending the invitation over the phone, email is acceptable. The more formal the event, the more paper still makes sense. Most couples land somewhere in between, and that is where this guide helps.

Is It OK to Send Wedding Invitations Online? What Experts Say

Etiquette has moved with the times, but it has not dropped its standards. The Emily Post Institute notes that just because you can send an email does not mean you should, and that formality is the deciding factor.

The Knot presents digital invitations as a good fit for many couples. It also gives a fair warning: some guests may not think a digital invitation is proper, and some simply love a paper card they can keep.

Even digital invitation companies agree that how you send matters most. Greenvelope, which sells online invitations, points to mass group emails as what makes an invitation feel tacky, and recommends sending each one to a named guest or household.

So the real question is not "digital or paper?" It is "how do I make a digital invitation feel like it was made for this guest?"

When Digital Works and When to Mix in Paper

When online wedding invitations are a great fit

Online wedding invitations work especially well in these cases:

- A relaxed or semi-formal wedding, such as a garden party or a small dinner
- Guests spread across several cities or countries
- A multi-day celebration with several events, like a mehndi, sangeet and reception
- A short timeline, where mail would eat up weeks
- A couple who wants RSVPs, maps and updates in one place

When to keep paper, or mix both

Paper still earns its place for a very formal or black-tie wedding. It also matters for guests who do not use email or smartphones much, and for anyone who will treasure a card in a frame or album.

Many couples do both. They mail a small number of printed invitations to grandparents and older relatives, and send the digital version to everyone else. This keeps the keepsake for the people who value it most, without printing and posting 150 cards.

Ask your parents or the oldest people on your list how they would like to be invited. One five-minute call can save hurt feelings later.

Digital Wedding Invitation Etiquette for Addressing Guests

Addressing is where digital wedding invitation etiquette matters most. On paper, the envelope tells guests exactly who is invited. Online, your message and the invitation itself have to do that job.

Names and households

Send each invitation to one person or one household. Use the names you would write on an envelope: "Dear Maria and James," not "Hi all." Never put your whole guest list in one email's To line, and never add guests to a group chat to invite them.

If your invitation tool supports personal links, use them. With Nimtto, personal guest links (each guest's own name on their invitation) are part of the Pro Max plan.

Plus-ones

Be specific. If a guest may bring someone, say so plainly in your message, and name the partner if you know them. If a guest is invited alone, address the message to them only, and do not mention a plus-one at all.

Children and adults-only weddings

The Emily Post Institute explains that the way an invitation is addressed shows exactly who is invited and, by leaving names out, who is not. It advises against writing "no children" on the invitation itself.

When children are invited, the Emily Post Institute suggests writing their names on a line below their parents' names. Online, that simply means naming each child in your message or on the invitation. For an adults-only wedding, address only the adults, and put a gentle note on your wedding website or in a personal message to parents.

Plus-one wording:
Dear [Name],
We would love for you and a guest to celebrate with us on [date].
When you RSVP, please add your guest's full name so we can include them on our seating plan.
With love,
[Your names]

Adults-only wording (personal message to parents):
Hi [Name],
We are so happy you and [Partner's name] can join us on [date].
We have planned our celebration as an adults-only evening, and we hope this gives you a relaxed night out.
Thank you for understanding. We cannot wait to see you both.
[Your names]

Timing: When to Send Online Wedding Invitations

Digital invitations arrive instantly, but guests still need the same notice. The Knot suggests sending invitations six to eight weeks before the wedding. Destination weddings and multi-day events need more notice, because guests have to plan travel and time off.

A common plan looks like this:

1. Save the date: several months ahead, so guests can block the dates
2. Invitation: about six to eight weeks ahead, with the full details and RSVP
3. RSVP deadline: a few weeks before the wedding, and before your caterer's final count is due
4. Reminder: about a week before the RSVP deadline, only to guests who have not replied

Our guide on when to send wedding invitations covers timelines for local, destination and multi-event weddings in more detail.

What to Include (and What to Leave on the Website)

Keep the invitation itself focused. The Knot recommends sticking to the essential details on the invitation and putting everything else on your wedding website.

A clear digital invitation includes:

- Your names, and the hosts' names if your parents are hosting
- The date and start time of each event
- The venue, with a map link
- Dress code, if you have one
- How and when to RSVP

The extras belong one tap away: hotel blocks, travel notes, parking, your story and photos. A digital invitation can hold all of this on one page. A Nimtto invitation, for example, includes every event with its time, venue and Google Maps link, plus travel notes and RSVP, as shown on the features page.

Registry mention etiquette

This is one rule that has not changed. The Emily Post Institute says a wedding invitation should never mention gifts or registry details, and that the wedding website is the right home for that information.

Online, follow the same spirit. Do not put a registry link in your invitation message. Let guests find it on your wedding website, or share it when someone asks. Nimtto does not run gift registries, so if you have one, link to it from the website section that guests explore on their own.

A classic pressed-card style digital wedding invitation shown on a phone

The Message to Send With Your Link

The note you send with the link is your envelope. It should be warm, short and personal. Our full guide to wedding invitation wording examples has invitation text for every style, but here is the message itself.

Message to send with the invitation link:
Dear [Name],
We are getting married! We would be so happy to have you with us on [date] in [city].
Your invitation, with all the details and the RSVP, is here:
[link]
Please reply by [RSVP date]. We hope to see you there.
With love,
[Your names]

Note to an older relative, offering a printed copy:
Dear [Aunt / Uncle / Grandma Name],
We sent our wedding invitation by email, but we would love for you to have a printed copy too.
We will mail one to you this week. If it is easier, you can reply by phone at [number].
We cannot wait to celebrate with you.
Love,
[Your names]

Send from your own email or phone number, with a clear subject line such as "Our wedding invitation: [Your names]." A message from an unknown sender is easy to ignore or lose to spam.

RSVP Deadline Etiquette and Polite Follow-Ups

Guests should reply by your deadline. That is basic etiquette for them. Your part is to make replying easy and the date impossible to miss.

Put the RSVP date in your message and on the invitation. Make the reply button easy to find. If guests can answer for several events, let them choose each one separately, so your mehndi count and your reception count stay accurate.

When the deadline passes, follow up kindly. Assume a busy week, not rudeness. Start with a short message, and call only if you still have not heard back a few days later. Our guide to collecting RSVPs online explains how to track replies and export your final list.

Gentle RSVP reminder:
Hi [Name]! Just a friendly note that we are finalizing numbers for [date].
If you have a moment, could you RSVP here by [new date]? [link]
No pressure at all if you cannot make it. We would just love to know.
Thank you!
[Your names]

Privacy and Changes of Plans

Keep the link off social media

An online invitation is still a private invitation. Do not post the link on Instagram, Facebook or a public story. Anyone who sees it can open it, and you may get replies from people you did not plan to host.

Share it only one-to-one or one-to-household. Ask close family not to forward it. If you want to celebrate publicly, post a photo of the design without the link.

When plans change

This is where paperless wedding invitations shine. If the venue, time or date changes, you update the invitation once and the same link shows the new details. No reprinting, and no second mailing.

Still tell guests directly. People will not open the link again unless something prompts them.

Change-of-plans update:
Hi [Name],
A quick update for our wedding: [the reception will now start at 7:00 pm / the venue has changed to New Venue].
The invitation has been updated with the new details and map: [link]
Your RSVP still stands, so there is nothing else you need to do.
Thank you, and see you soon!
[Your names]

E-Vite Wedding Etiquette: Do's and Don'ts

Here is a quick reference for e-vite wedding etiquette, so you can check your plan before you hit send.

| Do | Don't |
|---|---|
| Send to each guest or household by name | Send one mass email or group chat message |
| Match the design to how formal your wedding is | Use a casual template for a black-tie event |
| Say clearly who is invited, including plus-ones and children | Leave guests guessing whether they can bring someone |
| Put the RSVP date in your message and on the invitation | Hide the reply button below long text |
| Offer printed copies to older guests who prefer paper | Assume everyone checks email every day |
| Keep registry details on your website | Put a registry link in the invitation message |
| Keep the link private | Post the link on social media |
| Message guests when details change | Change the invitation quietly and hope they notice |
| Send thank-you notes after the wedding | Skip thank-yous because the invitation was digital |

Final Thoughts

Sending your wedding invitation online is good etiquette when you treat it like paper: addressed to a person, clear about who is invited, and sent with care. Add printed copies for the few guests who will treasure them, and you have covered everyone.

If you would like a digital invitation with RSVP, maps and every event in one link, browse the Nimtto designs, from the classic Letterpress to the modern Wax Seal and the soft Blush Roses. The pricing page lists each plan, starting at $49, paid once.
