### Are digital wedding invitations tacky?
Not when they are done with care. What reads as careless is a mass group email or a plain forwarded link. A well-designed invitation, sent to each guest by name with a short personal note, is widely accepted.

### Should I send a save the date and an invitation online, or just one?
Many couples send both: a save the date months ahead, then the full invitation closer to the day. If your wedding is local and the timeline is short, one invitation with a clear RSVP date can be enough.

### How do I send online wedding invitations to guests without smartphones?
Send those few guests a printed copy or a simple card in the mail, and give them a phone number to reply. You can also ask a family member who lives near them to show them the invitation.

### Is it OK to text a wedding invitation?
Yes, a text with a link to a real invitation is fine for most guests. Write a personal line first so it does not look like spam, and send it one person at a time rather than in a big group chat.

### Can guests RSVP for people who were not invited?
They may try, which is why clear addressing matters. With personal guest links, each invitation carries the guest's own name. Nimtto offers this on the [Pro Max plan](/international/pricing/).

### Do I still need to send paper thank-you notes after a digital wedding?
A digital invitation does not replace a proper thank-you. A handwritten or mailed note is still the warmest way to thank guests for gifts and for coming, so plan time for notes after the wedding.

### How long should the invitation stay online after the wedding?
Long enough for guests to revisit photos and details. Nimtto invitations stay online for at least one year after the event, with no subscription. See the [FAQ](/international/faq/) for more.

## How to Collect RSVPs Online: A Simple Guide for Couples
URL: https://nimtto.com/international/blog/how-to-collect-rsvps-online/
By Nimtto Team · Published 2026-10-18 · Updated 2026-10-18
Pick one place for replies, ask only what you need, and follow up kindly. Here is how to set up online RSVPs, with a tool comparison and wording you can copy.

Here is how to collect RSVPs online: choose one place where every guest replies, and put that link and a firm reply-by date on your invitation. Ask only what your caterer and seating plan need. Then send a friendly reminder before the deadline, and call anyone who still has not answered.

That is the whole method. This guide walks through how to collect RSVPs online without chasing people for weeks: which tool to pick, what to ask, how to word every message, and how to turn the replies into a clean list for your caterer.

Your Options for Online RSVP for a Wedding

There are five common ways couples take replies today. Most couples use one main tool, plus a phone number as a backup for guests who would rather call.

1. A wedding RSVP website form. Guests visit your wedding website, find their name and reply.
2. An invitation with built-in RSVP. The invitation itself carries the reply form, so guests read the details and answer in the same place. This is how a wedding invitation with RSVP from Nimtto works.
3. Google Forms. A form you build yourself, with the answers landing in a spreadsheet.
4. A spreadsheet plus messages. You send the invitation, guests text or email back, and you type each reply into a sheet.
5. A QR code on a printed card. A paper invitation with a digital RSVP. The code simply points to one of the options above.

How the options compare

| | Wedding website form | Invitation with built-in RSVP | Google Forms | Spreadsheet + messages | QR code on printed card |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Your effort | Medium: build the site, add your guest list | Low to medium: details are set up once | Medium: build and test the form yourself | High: every reply is typed by hand | Same as the tool it points to, plus printing |
| Guest experience | Open the site, search for a name, reply | Reply on the invitation they just read | A plain form that works on any phone | Easy for guests, they just text back | Scan, then the same as the tool it points to |
| Replies per event | Often available, check the plan | Varies; Nimtto shows replies per event | Yes, if you add a question per event | Only if guests say so, and you track it | Same as the tool it points to |
| Meal choices | Common feature | Varies, ask before you buy | Yes, you write the question | Only if guests remember to say | Same as the tool it points to |
| Plus-ones | Can be limited through the guest list | Party size per reply; some offer named guest links | Hard to limit, anyone with the link can add names | You decide case by case | Same as the tool it points to |
| Privacy | Account-based, check sharing settings | Replies go to your private dashboard | Anyone with the link can submit; keep the sheet private | Data spread across phones and inboxes | Same as the tool it points to |
| Cost | Basic plans are often free; check what is extra | A one-time or plan price | Free with a Google account | Free | Printing cost plus the tool it points to |

No single tool suits every wedding. If you host several events, replies per event matter most. If your list is small and close, a spreadsheet and a few texts may be all you need.

Pick one list as your source of truth. If a guest texts you a yes instead of using the form, add it to that same list right away. Two half-finished lists cause more mistakes than one messy one.

What to Ask on Your Wedding RSVP Website or Form

Zola suggests asking for meal choices inside the RSVP itself, not in a separate follow-up, because many guests answer the first request and skip the second. Keep the form short. Every extra question is one more reason to put it off.

Ask these:

- Full name of each person replying, so "Sam" is not a mystery on your seating chart.
- Attending, yes or no, for each event. If you host a welcome dinner, a ceremony and a reception, ask about each one separately.
- How many are coming, or the names of named guests. Show the number of seats you offered.
- Dietary needs or allergies. A short text box works well.
- A meal choice, only if you serve a plated dinner with options.
- A message to the couple (optional). Guests enjoy writing these, and you will enjoy reading them.
- A song request (optional). Fun, but never required.

Skip home addresses, birthdays and phone numbers unless you truly need them. You already have contact details if you sent the invitation, and less data means less to protect.

How to Handle Plus-Ones and Kids

This is where most RSVP confusion starts. The fix is to decide your rules before the invitations go out, then make the form match them.

Name the people you invite

The Emily Post Institute recommends using the real names of companions instead of a vague "and guest" whenever you know them, and listing invited children by name too. The same rule works online. The invitation should show exactly who is invited, so nobody has to guess.

Set a seat count for each reply

If your tool lets you set seats per household, use it. A couple sees two seats, not an open box. If your tool cannot limit numbers, as with a shared Google Form, write the number clearly in the message that carries the link.

Say it kindly when kids are not invited

Add one plain line to the invitation or website, then let the named seats do the work. If a guest still adds children, call them early and privately. A kind call beats a surprise at the door.

Line for an adults-only wedding:
We love your little ones, but our celebration
will be adults only. Thank you for understanding,
and we hope you enjoy a night out with us!

How to Set Your RSVP Deadline

The Knot says wedding RSVPs should be due at least four weeks before the wedding, and no later than two weeks before. The easiest way to pick a date is to work backward. Ask your caterer when they need the final count, then set your deadline a week or so before that, which leaves time for follow-up calls.

Give guests who must fly in more time. The Knot's destination wedding advice suggests an earlier reply date for remote locations, in some cases at least three months before the wedding. For the invitation timeline itself, see our guide on when to send wedding invitations.

Always write a real date with the weekday, such as "Saturday, May 1". A phrase like "as soon as possible" has no end, so nobody acts on it.

Wording for Your Digital RSVP Messages

Put the RSVP link in the same message as the invitation. A separate "oh, and please RSVP" note is easy to miss. Our digital wedding invitation etiquette guide has more on sending invitations by text, email and WhatsApp.

RSVP line on the invitation:
Kindly reply by Saturday, May 1
using the RSVP button on this invitation.
We have reserved [2] seats in your honor.

Message that carries the RSVP link:
Hi [Guest's name]! We're getting married on [Saturday, June 12] in [City], and we would love to have you there.
Here is our invitation with all the details: [link]
Please reply on the invitation by [Saturday, May 1] so we can give our caterer a final count.
With love, [Partner 1] and [Partner 2]

Note for guests who prefer to reply by phone:
Rather reply by phone? Call or text [Helper's name]
at [phone number] by [Saturday, May 1],
and we'll add your answer for you.

That phone note matters more than it looks. Grandparents and busy relatives often reply faster to a person than to a form. Choose one helper, such as a parent or a sibling, and ask them to add every phone reply to the main list the same day.

Reminders and Chasing Non-Responders

Plan two written reminders. Send the first about ten days before the deadline, only to guests who have not replied yet. Send the final one a day or two before the deadline.

Friendly reminder (about 10 days before the deadline):
Hi [Name]! Just a gentle reminder that RSVPs for our wedding are due on [Saturday, May 1].
You can reply right here: [link]
It only takes a moment. We really hope you can make it!

Final reminder (1 to 2 days before the deadline):
Hi [Name], our caterer needs final numbers this week, so we're closing RSVPs on [Saturday, May 1].
Could you let us know if you can join us? [link]
If it's easier, just reply to this message with yes or no and how many.

After the deadline, pick up the phone. The Emily Post Institute says it is perfectly polite for hosts to call and ask whether a guest plans to attend. Keep the call warm and short. Most late repliers are busy, not rude.

If your list is long, share the calls. Each family takes its own relatives, and the two of you take your friends. Note every answer in the main list before the end of the day.

When someone does reply, thank them. It takes a minute and it sets a happy tone for the day.

Thank-you after a guest replies:
Thank you for replying, [Name]! We're so happy you'll be there.
We'll send parking and timing details closer to the day.
If anything changes, just let us know.

(If they can't come)
Thank you for letting us know, [Name]. We'll miss you,
and we'll share photos with you after the wedding.

RSVP Tracking: Keep One Clean List

Good RSVP tracking answers three questions at a glance: who is coming, how many, and to which events. Check the list once a week, not every hour. Constant checking adds stress and changes nothing.

These columns cover almost every wedding:

| Column | What goes in it |
|---|---|
| Household name | As written on the invitation |
| Seats offered | The number of people you invited |
| Seats confirmed | The number who said yes |
| Events | Yes or no for each event |
| Dietary needs | Allergies, meal choice, children's meals |
| Side | Which family or friend group they belong to |
| Follow-up | Who will call them if they have not replied |

The "Follow-up" column is the one most couples forget. It turns a long list of silent guests into a short job for each helper.

Exporting the List for the Caterer and Seating Chart

Once the deadline passes, turn your replies into a few simple lists. Most online tools let you download a spreadsheet. With Nimtto, your family sees every reply in the dashboard (who is coming, how many and which events) and can export the replies when you need them.

From that export, make:

1. A caterer sheet. Total guests per event, plus every dietary need with the guest's name and, later, the table number.
2. A seating sheet. Sort by side and household, then build your tables. Keep households together.
3. A venue count. Chairs, place settings and any high chairs for each event.
4. A check-in list. An alphabetical list for whoever greets guests at the door.

Send the caterer sheet as soon as it is ready, then send one final update if anything changes. Changing numbers again and again makes mistakes more likely.

Keeping Guest Data Private

Your RSVP list holds names, dietary and health details, and sometimes children's names. Treat it with care.

- Share the sheet with as few people as possible. Give edit access only to helpers who need it, and never post the sheet link in a group chat.
- Collect only what you need. If you do not use a question, remove it.
- Watch open forms. Anyone with a public form link can submit a reply, so check for duplicates and names you do not know.
- Use personal links when you can. On Nimtto's Pro Max plan, each guest gets a personal link with their own name on the invitation, which makes it clear who is replying.
- Clean up after the wedding. Remove helpers' access and delete what you no longer need once thank-you notes are done.

Never ask for passport numbers, payment details or home security information (such as "we will be away on these dates") in an RSVP form. A wedding RSVP never needs them.

The Olive Grove wedding invitation open on a phone, with a watercolor olive wreath and the couple's names

How to Collect RSVPs Online, in Short

Collecting RSVPs online works best when it is simple for guests: one link, a short form, a clear date and a kind reminder. Decide your plus-one rules first, set the deadline from your caterer's date, and keep every answer in one list.

If you would like the invitation and the RSVP in one place, look through our designs, such as Olive Grove, Wildflower and Garden Party. You pay once, with no charge per guest, and our pricing page shows what each plan includes.

### What is the easiest way to collect wedding RSVPs online?
Use one reply channel that lives where guests already are: a form on your invitation or wedding website, sent as a link by text or email. Give a phone number as a backup for guests who would rather call.

### Is it rude to ask guests to RSVP online only?
No. Online replies are normal now. It is kind, though, to name one person guests can call or text instead, so older relatives and less online friends are not left out.

### How do I stop guests from adding extra people to their RSVP?
Name every invited person on the invitation and set a seat count for each household if your tool allows it. If someone still adds a guest, call them privately and explain that your numbers are fixed.

### Can guests reply to some wedding events and not others?
Yes, if you ask about each event separately. A welcome dinner, ceremony and reception should each get their own yes or no, so your counts are right for every venue.

### What should I do if a guest replies after the RSVP deadline?
If your caterer can still change the count, say yes warmly and add them. If numbers are already locked, call them, thank them, and explain gently that the final count has gone in.

### Can I put a QR code for RSVPs on a printed invitation?
Yes. Print the code large enough to scan, test it on two or three phones, and print the short web address under it too, for guests whose camera will not read it.

### Does a Nimtto invitation include RSVP?
Yes. Guests reply on the invitation itself, and you see who is coming, how many and which events in your dashboard, which you can export. See [what each plan includes](/international/pricing/).

## Nepali and South Asian Weddings in the USA: Invitations for Families Near and Far
URL: https://nimtto.com/international/blog/nepali-south-asian-weddings-usa/
By Nimtto Team · Published 2026-10-18 · Updated 2026-10-18
Several events, two scripts and family spread across time zones. Here is how to write one invitation that works for guests in the USA, Nepal, India and beyond.

South Asian wedding invitations in the USA have a bigger job than most. They need to show several events, each with its own time, venue, dress note and guest list. They also need to reach relatives in Nepal, India, the UK or the Gulf, who live in other time zones and may need months to plan the trip.

The simple answer: send one clear invitation with a section for every event, and write times in the venue's local time. Add home-country times in your messages to family abroad. Invite overseas guests 8 to 12 months ahead, and call your elders before you send the link.

South Asian Wedding Invitations in the USA: One Invitation, Many Events

A Nepali or South Asian wedding is rarely one event. It is often a series across two to four days, and many guests are invited to only some of them. Even in Nepal, Republica reports that haldi, mehendi and sangeet have become common parts of the wedding week, alongside older family rituals.

Not every guest knows every term. Your friends from work may never have been to a mehndi. A one-line explanation next to each event name helps them feel welcome, not lost.

| Event | What it is, in one line | Who is usually invited | Dress note idea |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mehndi (mehendi) | Henna is painted on the bride's hands, with music and food | Close family and friends | Bright colors, easy sleeves |
| Haldi | Family apply turmeric paste to the couple for a glowing start | Close family | Yellow, and clothes you do not mind staining |
| Sangeet | An evening of music, dance and family performances | Family and friends | Festive, dressy and comfortable to dance in |
| Baraat or janti | The groom's side arrives in a lively procession with music | The groom's family and friends | Festive, with shoes for walking |
| Wedding ceremony | The marriage rituals, led by the families | Family and invited guests | Traditional or formal |
| Reception | Dinner and celebration, often the biggest guest list | Everyone invited | Formal or cocktail |

In Nepali families, janti is the word for the groom's party that travels to the wedding. Many families in the USA use "baraat" and "janti" side by side so both sides of the family recognize it.

Keep each explanation to one line. The goal is to help a guest show up at the right place in the right clothes, not to write a history lesson.

How to Write a Multi-Day Wedding Invitation

For a multi-day wedding invitation, give every event the same set of details in the same order. Guests scan for times and places, so a steady layout saves them from rereading.

For each event, include:

1. The event name with its one-line explanation.
2. Day and date, with the weekday.
3. Start time, and an "arrive by" time if the event starts with a procession or a set moment.
4. Venue name and address, with a map link.
5. A dress note.
6. Who is invited, if not everyone.

An Indian wedding invitation website does this well, because each event gets its own section with its own map. A Nimtto invitation, for example, lists every event with its time, venue and a Google Maps link. A printed card struggles to fit five events and still look calm.

Multi-event invitation summary:
With the blessings of our families,
[Bride's name] and [Groom's name]
invite you to celebrate their wedding

Mehndi: Thursday, June 10, 5:00 PM
[Venue], [City]

Sangeet: Friday, June 11, 7:00 PM
[Venue], [City]

Baraat and Wedding Ceremony: Saturday, June 12
Baraat begins at 9:30 AM, ceremony at 10:30 AM
[Venue], [City]

Reception: Saturday, June 12, 6:30 PM
[Venue], [City]

Please reply by Saturday, May 1

Dress code line:
Mehndi: bright colors, comfortable for sitting on cushions
Sangeet: festive and ready to dance
Ceremony: traditional or formal wear
Reception: formal, with shoes for the dance floor

Who Is Invited to Which Events

The trickiest part is the guest list. Your aunt is invited to everything. A colleague may be invited only to the reception. The invitation should make that clear without making anyone feel second-tier.

The cleanest way is to send each guest group a version that shows only their events. A reception guest then sees a full, happy invitation to the reception, not a list of things they are left out of. Ask your invitation service how it handles this before you order. If it cannot, send reception guests their own message or card.

Track replies per event, too. Our guide on how to collect RSVPs online explains how to ask about each event separately, so your caterer gets the right count for every night.

Wording for guests invited only to the reception:
Together with their families,
[Bride's name] and [Groom's name]
request the pleasure of your company
at their wedding reception

Saturday, June 12, 6:30 PM
[Venue], [City]
Dinner, music and dancing to follow

Event-specific invite for a sangeet or mehndi:
You're invited to the Sangeet!
An evening of music, dance and family performances
to celebrate [Bride's name] and [Groom's name]

Friday, June 11, 7:00 PM
[Venue], [City]
Come dressed to dance. Dinner will be served.

A Nepali Wedding in the USA: Names and Dates in Two Scripts

Many families planning a Nepali wedding in the USA want both English and Nepali on the invitation. English helps friends and colleagues. Devanagari speaks to grandparents and relatives back home, and it feels like a real family invitation.

A few rules keep two scripts tidy:

- Use the same order in both scripts. If the bride's name comes first in English, it comes first in Nepali too.
- Never machine-translate names. Ask a parent or grandparent to spell every name in Devanagari, then check it again before guests see it.
- Keep the English date simple. Write "Saturday, June 12, 2027" in English. Many Nepali families also like to add the Bikram Sambat date, so ask an elder to confirm the correct conversion.
- Do not cram. If both scripts make a section crowded, put the Nepali text in its own short block.

Nimtto's Nepali wedding invitations come in English and Nepali, and a real designer reviews the text with you before any guest sees it.

The Laali wedding invitation on a phone, in blush pink and gold with lanterns

Wedding Invitations for Family Abroad: Time Zones

Wedding invitations for family abroad should always list times in the venue's local time. Then, in the message you send to each relative, add one line with their own local time. This matters most for calls, video chats with family who cannot travel, and any moment you want them to share from home.

Nepal is on UTC+5:45 and has never used daylight saving time, according to timeanddate. India stays on UTC+5:30 all year, as does the UAE on UTC+4. The USA, however, changes its clocks. In 2027, US daylight saving time runs from March 14 to November 7, per timeanddate, so the gap to Nepal or India changes by one hour twice a year.

| Place | UTC offset | Daylight saving? | When it is 6:00 PM in New York in June | When it is 6:00 PM in New York in January |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| New York (ET) | UTC-5, or UTC-4 in summer | Yes | 6:00 PM | 6:00 PM |
| Chicago (CT) | UTC-6, or UTC-5 in summer | Yes | 5:00 PM | 5:00 PM |
| Los Angeles (PT) | UTC-8, or UTC-7 in summer | Yes | 3:00 PM | 3:00 PM |
| London (UK) | UTC+0, or UTC+1 in summer | Yes | 11:00 PM | 11:00 PM |
| Dubai (UAE) | UTC+4 | No | 2:00 AM next day | 3:00 AM next day |
| New Delhi (India) | UTC+5:30 | No | 3:30 AM next day | 4:30 AM next day |
| Kathmandu (Nepal) | UTC+5:45 | No | 3:45 AM next day | 4:45 AM next day |

Two details catch families out:

- The UK and US change clocks on different days. UK clocks go forward on the last Sunday in March and back on the last Sunday in October, says GOV.UK. For a few weeks each spring and fall, London is four hours ahead of New York instead of five.
- An evening in the USA is early morning in South Asia. A 6:00 PM reception in New York starts before dawn in Kathmandu. Plan any call with grandparents for a morning or lunch event instead.

Arizona (most of the state) and Hawaii do not use daylight saving time. If your wedding is there, check the gap for your exact date on a time zone converter.

Inviting Overseas Guests Early: Visas and Letters

Relatives from Nepal, India and many other countries need a US visitor visa (B-2) to attend. Visiting friends or relatives is one of the purposes the US State Department's visitor visa page lists for this visa, but the process takes time, and interview waits differ by city.

That is why timing matters. The Knot suggests sending destination wedding save-the-dates earlier than usual when guests travel far, and 8 to 12 months is a fair target for family overseas. Share the date the moment it is fixed, even before the full invitation is ready. Your relatives can then check the State Department's current visa appointment wait times for their city.

What about an invitation letter?

Many families ask for one. Here the State Department is clear: its visitor visa page says a letter of invitation or affidavit of support is not needed to apply, and it is not one of the factors used to decide whether to issue or deny the visa. Applicants must qualify on their own ties to their home country.

So a letter will not hurt, but it will not guarantee a visa either. If a relative still wants one, keep it short and true: who you are, your relationship, the wedding dates and city, and your contact details.

Visa rules can change. Ask your relatives to read the official page and their local US embassy's instructions before the interview, and never promise anyone that a visa is certain.

Elders Who Expect a Call or a Card

For many families, a link alone feels too casual for grandparents, senior relatives and family friends of your parents' generation. The respectful order is simple: a parent calls first, then the link follows.

A few habits help:

- Let parents make the elder calls. It carries more weight from them than from the couple.
- Send the link right after the call, so they have the details in hand.
- Print a handful of cards for the elders who truly expect paper. Most guests can still get the digital invitation.
- Offer help to open it. A cousin nearby can show a grandparent the invitation and reply on their behalf.

Message to family in Nepal:
Namaste [Name] ji,
हाम्रो शुभविवाहमा सपरिवार पाल्नुहुन हार्दिक निमन्त्रणा गर्दछौं।
[Bride's name] and [Groom's name] are getting married on Saturday, June 12, in [City], USA.
The ceremony starts at 10:30 AM [City] time, which is [8:15 PM] Nepal time.
All the details are here: [link]
We hope to see you, and we would love your blessings.

Note for elders:
Respected [Name] ji,
It would mean so much to us to have your blessings.
Mummy and Buwa will call you to share the details.
The invitation link below has every date and place.
If you need any help, [Cousin's name] will be happy to help you reply.

Sending by WhatsApp and Viber

WhatsApp and Viber are how most South Asian families already talk, so they are the natural way to send. With Nimtto, guests open one link with no app download or account needed, which suits relatives of every age.

- Send personal messages, not one giant group post. A message with the guest's own name feels like an invitation. A group forward feels like an announcement.
- Use the right app for each relative. Some relatives in Nepal use Viber more than WhatsApp. Ask your parents which app each household checks.
- Add a voice note for elders. A short spoken invitation from a parent is warm and easy to understand.
- Send at a sensible local hour. Use the table above, so a message does not ping someone at 3:00 AM.

For more ready-made lines, see our wedding invitation wording examples.

Bringing It All Together

A Nepali or South Asian wedding in the USA brings together guests from many places. Your invitation can make that easy: one section per event, one-line explanations, clear dress notes, times your relatives can read at a glance, and an early date for anyone who needs a visa.

If you want all of this in one link, look at designs like Laali, Mahal, Mehendi and Swayambar. See how we help couples in the USA, and check our pricing: you pay once, with no subscription and no charge per guest.

### How early should we invite relatives from Nepal or India to a wedding in the USA?
Tell them the date as soon as it is fixed, ideally 8 to 12 months ahead. Visitor visa appointments can take time, so a late invitation can mean a relative simply cannot get there.

### Do relatives need an invitation letter for a US visitor visa?
The US State Department says a letter of invitation is not needed to apply for a visitor visa and is not a factor in the decision. Officers look at the applicant's own ties to their home country.

### Should we send one invitation for all events or separate ones?
One invitation with a clear section for each event is easiest for guests. If some guests are invited only to the reception, give them a version that shows only the events they are invited to.

### What time zone should a wedding invitation use for guests abroad?
Always print event times in the venue's local time. In the message you send to family abroad, add one line with the time back home, such as Nepal time, so nobody has to work it out.

### Is it okay to send a wedding invitation to elders by WhatsApp?
Yes, many families do, but call first. A personal call from a parent, followed by the link, shows the respect elders expect and makes sure they know to open it.

### Can the invitation be in both English and Nepali?
Yes. Nimtto invitations come in English and Nepali, so names, dates and greetings can appear in both. Ask a family member to check the Devanagari spelling of every name before guests see it.

### What should a dress code line say for a multi-day wedding?
Give one short note per event, such as bright colors for the mehndi or formal wear for the reception. Mention comfortable shoes for outdoor events or a long procession.

## Wedding Invitation Wording Examples for Every Situation
URL: https://nimtto.com/international/blog/wedding-invitation-wording-examples/
By Nimtto Team · Published 2026-10-18 · Updated 2026-10-18
Nineteen copy-ready wording examples, from classic formal lines to a courthouse wedding with a party later, plus the simple rules that keep any invitation clear and correct.

The best wedding invitation wording examples share one plan: who is hosting, a line asking guests to come, your names, the date and time, the place, and how to reply. Formal wording spells everything out in words. Casual wording keeps the same order but sounds like you talking.

Below you will find the anatomy of an invitation, the formal rules most etiquette guides agree on, and 19 copy-ready examples. They cover parents hosting, the couple hosting, divorced parents, a parent who has passed, small weddings, destination trips, courthouse ceremonies and online invitations.

The Anatomy of a Wedding Invitation

Every invitation, formal or relaxed, follows the same basic order. The Knot suggests keeping the main card to the essentials and moving extra details to an enclosure card or wedding website. Here is what each line does.

| Line | What it says | Formal example | Casual example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Host line | Who is inviting | Mr. and Mrs. David Carter | Together with their families |
| Request line | The ask | request the pleasure of your company | invite you to celebrate |
| Couple | Your names | Emma Rose Carter and James Lee Park | Emma and James |
| Date | Day, date, year | Saturday, the twelfth of June, two thousand twenty-seven | Saturday, June 12, 2027 |
| Time | Start time | at half after four o'clock | at 4:30 p.m. |
| Venue | Place and city | The Glasshouse, Portland, Oregon | The Glasshouse, Portland |
| Reception line | What comes next | Dinner and dancing to follow | Party to follow! |
| RSVP | How and when to reply | The favor of a reply is requested by the fifteenth of May | Please reply by May 15 |

You can drop the host line on a casual invitation. Everything else should stay, because guests need it to plan.

Formal Wedding Invitation Wording Rules

Formal wedding invitation wording has a few set habits. You do not have to follow all of them, but knowing them helps you break them on purpose.

"Honor of your presence" or "pleasure of your company"

Emily Post treats "the honour of your presence" as the most solemn request and ties it to the type of ceremony setting. "The pleasure of your company" is the traditional choice for venues such as hotels, gardens, homes and event halls. Emily Post also keeps the British "u" in "honour". Many American couples write "honor", which is just as correct. Choose one spelling and stick with it.

Dates and times in words

Formal invitations write the date, the year and the time in words. Emily Post prefers "half after four o'clock" to "half past" or "four-thirty", and leaves "and" out of the year ("two thousand twenty-seven"). WeddingWire accepts "half past" and adds "in the afternoon" or "in the morning" where it helps. Both are fine. Just be consistent.

When to use "and" between names

"And" tells the reader that two people are married or marrying. That is why Minted and WeddingWire both advise putting divorced parents on separate lines with no "and" between them. When one family hosts, many invitations join the couple with "to" ("their daughter Emma Rose to James Lee Park"). When both families or the couple host, "and" is the usual choice.

Names and titles

Use full names on formal invitations, including middle names if you like. Emily Post abbreviates titles such as "Mr." and "Mrs." but writes out "Doctor" when it fits on the line. Keep both partners' names in the same style: two full names, or two first names, never one of each.

Read your wording out loud before you print or publish it. If a line sounds stiff when you say it, your guests will hear it that way too.

Formal and Traditional Wording Examples

These examples follow formal wedding invitation wording. Swap in your own names, date and venue.

Formal invitation from the bride's parents:
Mr. and Mrs. David Carter
request the pleasure of your company
at the marriage of their daughter
Emma Rose
to
James Lee Park
Saturday, the twelfth of June
two thousand twenty-seven
at half after four o'clock
The Glasshouse
Portland, Oregon
Dinner and dancing to follow

Formal invitation from both sets of parents:
Mr. and Mrs. David Carter
and
Mr. and Mrs. Daniel Park
request the pleasure of your company
at the marriage of their children
Emma Rose Carter
and
James Lee Park
Saturday, the twelfth of June
two thousand twenty-seven
at half after four o'clock
The Glasshouse
Portland, Oregon

Divorced parents wedding invitation wording

Each parent gets their own line, with no "and" between them. A stepparent shares a line with the parent they are married to, as WeddingWire explains. Minted notes that the mother is usually listed first.

Divorced and remarried parents hosting:
Mrs. Linda Moore
Mr. and Mrs. David Carter
request the pleasure of your company
at the marriage of their daughter
Emma Rose Carter
to
James Lee Park
Saturday, the twelfth of June
two thousand twenty-seven
at four o'clock in the afternoon
The Glasshouse
Portland, Oregon

A parent who has passed

Etiquette guides agree that a parent who has died cannot be named as a host. You can still name them gently beside their child's name, using "the late" as WeddingWire suggests, or simply "daughter of".

Honoring a parent who has passed:
Mrs. Linda Carter
requests the pleasure of your company
at the marriage of her daughter
Emma Rose Carter
daughter of the late David Carter
to
James Lee Park
Saturday, the twelfth of June
two thousand twenty-seven
at half after four o'clock
The Glasshouse
Portland, Oregon

If naming a parent on the invitation feels too heavy, honor them another way: a line on your invitation website, a reserved seat, or a quiet moment in the speeches. The invitation itself can simply say "Together with their families".

Wedding Invitation Wording From the Bride and Groom

More couples host their own weddings now. In that case you can open with your own names, or with a shared line. WeddingWire suggests "Together with their families" when the couple and parents host together.

From the couple, formal:
Emma Rose Carter
and
James Lee Park
request the pleasure of your company
at their marriage
Saturday, the twelfth of June
two thousand twenty-seven
at half after four o'clock
The Glasshouse
Portland, Oregon

From the couple, with their families:
Together with their families
Emma Carter and James Park
invite you to celebrate their wedding
Saturday, June 12, 2027
at 4:30 p.m.
The Glasshouse, Portland, Oregon
Dinner and dancing to follow

Same-sex couple

The wording does not need to change at all. For name order, Minted suggests alphabetical order or whatever looks best in the design.

Same-sex couple:
Together with their families
Daniel Brooks
and
Marcus Reyes
invite you to celebrate their marriage
Saturday, the fourth of September
two thousand twenty-seven
at five o'clock in the evening
Willow Creek Farm
Asheville, North Carolina

Second wedding or vow renewal

For a second marriage, the couple usually hosts, and the tone can be warm and grown-up. A vow renewal says "renewal of vows" or "celebrate ten years" so no one thinks it is a first wedding.

Second wedding:
Laura Bennett and Michael Grant
joyfully invite you to their wedding
Saturday, October 16, 2027
at 3:00 p.m.
The Garden Room, Napa, California
A family dinner will follow

Vow renewal:
Ten years, two kids and one very old dog later
Sara and Tom Alvarez
invite you to celebrate the renewal of their vows
Saturday, August 21, 2027
at 6:00 p.m.
Harbor House, Seattle, Washington
Dinner and dancing to follow

Casual and Modern Wedding Invitation Wording

Casual wedding invitation wording keeps the same facts but drops the formal phrases. Emily Post notes that less formal couples can write naturally instead of using the set lines.

Casual:
We're getting married!
Emma and James
would love for you to join us
Saturday, June 12, 2027, at 4:30 p.m.
The Glasshouse, Portland
Food, drinks and dancing to follow

Modern and minimal:
Emma + James
June 12, 2027
4:30 p.m. ceremony
6:00 p.m. dinner and dancing
The Glasshouse, Portland
Come celebrate with us

Small and intimate:
We're keeping it small, and we want you there.
Emma and James
invite you to their wedding
Saturday, June 12, 2027, at 1:00 p.m.
Lunch to follow at Juniper Kitchen, Portland

Adults-only wedding

Zola says the clearest signal is addressing the invitation only to the people invited, and warns that a bare "adults only" can read as harsher than you mean. A kind line works better.

Adults-only line:
We love your little ones, but our celebration
will be for adults only.
Thank you for understanding, and enjoy a night off!

Wording for Special Situations

Destination wedding

Give guests the place and dates up front, because they will be booking travel.

Destination wedding:
Pack your bags!
Emma Carter and James Park
invite you to join them for their wedding
Saturday, June 12, 2027
Villa Rosa, Positano, Italy
Travel and hotel details are on our wedding website
Please reply by March 15, 2027

Courthouse wedding with a party later

Zola advises making it clear that you are already married, so guests know they are coming to a celebration, not a ceremony.

Courthouse wedding, party later:
We said "I do" at City Hall!
Now we want to celebrate with the people we love.
Emma and James Park
invite you to their wedding party
Saturday, August 7, 2027, at 7:00 p.m.
The Loft, Portland, Oregon
Dinner, drinks and dancing

Reception-only invitation

The Knot suggests a small change to the request line, such as "to celebrate the wedding of", when guests are invited to the reception only.

Reception only:
Mr. and Mrs. David Carter
request the pleasure of your company
at a reception to celebrate the marriage of
Emma Rose Carter and James Lee Park
Saturday, the twelfth of June
two thousand twenty-seven
at seven o'clock in the evening
The Glasshouse
Portland, Oregon

Multi-day wedding weekend

When every guest is invited to every event, Zola recommends an itinerary with each event's date, time, place and dress. Keep each entry short.

Wedding weekend itinerary:
We would love for you to join us all weekend.

Friday, June 11
Welcome dinner, 7:00 p.m.
Rooftop at The Marlow, Portland
Smart casual

Saturday, June 12
Ceremony, 4:30 p.m., followed by dinner and dancing
The Glasshouse, Portland
Formal

Sunday, June 13
Farewell brunch, 10:30 a.m.
Garden Cafe, Portland
Come as you are

If some guests are invited to only some events, send separate details so no one sees an event they are not invited to. An online invitation with an RSVP for each event, like a wedding invitation with RSVP, makes this easier to manage.

Wording for Online Invitations and Bilingual Guests

If half your guests speak another language, a short note in that language shows care. Put it near the top, not hidden at the end.

Bilingual note line:
English and Spanish details are both below.
Los detalles en español están abajo.

When you send an online invitation, the message you write with the link matters as much as the invitation. Keep it short and personal.

Message to send with an online invitation link:
Hi [Guest's name]!
We're getting married on Saturday, June 12, 2027, in Portland, and we'd love for you to be there.
Here's our invitation with all the details: [link]
Please reply on the invitation by May 15.
With love, Emma and James

With Nimtto, guests open one link and reply right on the invitation, so this message is all they need. For more on tone and timing, read our online invitation etiquette guide.

A classic letterpress style wedding invitation shown on a phone screen

Common Wording Mistakes to Avoid

- Mixing styles. Formal words with a numeric date, or one full name next to one nickname, looks unplanned.
- Too much on the main card. Registry, dress code essays and hotel blocks belong on a details card or website.
- No RSVP date. Always give a clear reply-by date. Our guide on when to send wedding invitations explains how to pick it.
- Unclear guest names. If children or plus-ones are not invited, address the invitation clearly instead of leaving guests to guess.
- Skipping the proofread. Check every name spelling, the day of the week against the date, and the venue address.

Final Thoughts

Good wedding invitation wording is clear first and pretty second. Pick the tone that fits your day, keep the order guests expect, and use the examples above as a starting point you can make your own.

If you want your wording on an animated invitation website, Nimtto's designers set up every line with you before guests see it. Browse the wedding invitation designs, such as the classic Letterpress, or see the pricing: you pay once, with no charge per guest.

### Who is traditionally named first on a wedding invitation?
The hosts come first, because they are the ones doing the inviting. Traditionally that was the bride's parents, but today it can be both families, the couple, or a line such as "Together with their families".

### Is it "honor" or "honour" on an American wedding invitation?
Both are seen. Emily Post keeps the British spelling "honour" for formal invitations, while many American couples use "honor". Pick one and use it the same way across all your wedding paper and pages.

### Do I need to write the year on a wedding invitation?
On a formal invitation the year is usually written out in words. On a casual or online invitation it is fine to leave it off or use numerals, since guests know which year you mean.

### How do I word an invitation if the couple is paying for the wedding?
Start with your own names, or use a warm opener such as "Together with their families". You do not need to name anyone as host if you are hosting yourselves.

### Should I put "no kids" on the wedding invitation?
Most etiquette guides say the clearest signal is how you address the invitation: name only the people invited. Add a gentle line on the details page or invitation website, rather than a blunt "no kids" on the main card.

### Can I put my registry on the wedding invitation?
Traditional etiquette keeps gift details off the main invitation. Put them on your wedding website or details page instead, where guests can find them if they want to.

### What should I write when I send an online wedding invitation?
Write a short personal message with the guest's name, one line about the day, the link, and the RSVP date. See our guide to [online invitation etiquette](/international/blog/digital-wedding-invitation-etiquette/) for more on tone and timing.

## When to Send Wedding Invitations and Save the Dates (Timeline)
URL: https://nimtto.com/international/blog/when-to-send-wedding-invitations/
By Nimtto Team · Published 2026-10-18 · Updated 2026-10-18
A clear month-by-month wedding invitation timeline, with the extra lead time destination, holiday and international guests need, plus reminder wording you can copy.

The usual answer to when to send wedding invitations is six to eight weeks before a local wedding, with save the dates going out six to eight months before. Set your RSVP deadline about three to four weeks before the wedding. That is the common guidance from Emily Post and The Knot.

For a destination wedding, a holiday weekend, or many guests flying in from abroad, add time at every step: save the dates eight to twelve months out, and invitations two to four months out. The rest of this guide explains why, and what to do if you are already behind.

The Short Answer: When to Send Wedding Invitations

Here is the standard plan for a local wedding, with the source for each step.

- Save the dates: 6 to 8 months before. The Knot suggests this window and says no later than six months if you can. Emily Post's planning timeline is a little looser, starting at three to six months or earlier.
- Invitations: 6 to 8 weeks before. Both Emily Post and The Knot use this window.
- RSVP deadline: 3 to 4 weeks before. The Knot's RSVP guide says at least four weeks out is ideal and no later than two weeks.

Why these numbers? Six to eight weeks gives guests about a month to reply. You then have a few weeks to give your caterer a final count and finish the seating plan.

Wedding Invitation Timeline, Month by Month

Use this wedding invitation timeline as a checklist. The right-hand column shows how things shift when guests travel.

| When | Local wedding | Destination or travel-heavy wedding |
|---|---|---|
| 12 to 9 months before | Set the date, start the guest list | Send save the dates (8 to 12 months is common) |
| 8 to 6 months before | Send save the dates | Wedding website live with travel and hotel notes |
| 5 to 4 months before | Wedding website live; choose your invitation design | Earliest window for invitations if travel is hard |
| 3 months before | Finalize the guest list and addresses | Send invitations (about 10 to 12 weeks or earlier) |
| 10 to 8 weeks before | Prepare invitations; send early to far-away guests | RSVP deadline for remote or peak-season trips |
| 8 to 6 weeks before | Send invitations | First reminder to guests who have not replied |
| 5 weeks before | First RSVP reminder (one week before the deadline) | Confirm counts for hotels and transport |
| 4 to 3 weeks before | RSVP deadline | Final reminders and calls |
| 3 to 2 weeks before | Final reminder, then phone the stragglers | Give final numbers to vendors |
| 1 week before | Send an update message with last details | Send an update message with arrival details |

The destination column draws on The Knot's guidance on destination wedding invitations: save the dates eight to twelve months out, invitations closer to ten or twelve weeks, and an RSVP deadline at least eight to ten weeks before for planners who need hotel numbers early. Some planners quoted there send invitations four to six months ahead so guests can book rooms and ask for time off.

Anyone who receives a save the date must also receive an invitation, as The Knot points out. Only send save the dates once your guest list is firm.

When to Send Save the Dates

Save the dates are optional, but they matter most when guests must travel, book leave or plan around a busy season. They only need your names, the date, the city, and a note that an invitation will follow. You do not need final venue details yet.

Do not go too early, though. The Knot advises against sending them more than a year ahead, because guests tend to forget or lose the details.

Special Cases: Destination, Holiday and International Guests

The standard numbers assume most guests live nearby. Adjust them for these situations. The local and destination rows follow the sources in this guide; the other rows are our practical suggestions built from them.

| Situation | Save the dates | Invitations | RSVP due |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local wedding | 6 to 8 months | 6 to 8 weeks | 3 to 4 weeks before |
| Holiday weekend | Closer to 8 months | 8 weeks or a little earlier | 4 weeks before |
| Destination wedding | 8 to 12 months | 10 to 12 weeks, or up to 4 to 6 months | 8 to 10 weeks before |
| Many guests from abroad | 9 to 12 months | 3 to 4 months | 6 to 8 weeks before |
| Multi-event weekend | Same as the main wedding | One invitation with every event | Same deadline for all events |

Holiday weekends

Flights and hotels fill up fast around long weekends. The Knot's save the date guide suggests leaning toward eight months for a holiday weekend or a far-flung location.

Destination wedding invitation timeline

Guests may need to book flights, rooms and time off, and sometimes renew a passport. That is why the destination wedding invitation timeline starts so early, and why the RSVP date is earlier too. Hotel room blocks often have their own release dates, so check your contracts and set your deadline before them.

International guests

Guests crossing borders need paperwork time. The U.S. State Department lists routine passport processing at about four to six weeks, plus mailing time. Guests who need a visa should check the Global Visa Wait Times page for their nearest embassy, because waits vary by city and the estimate does not include processing. Send these guests their save the date as early as you can, and tell them the date personally.

Multi-event weddings

If you are hosting a welcome dinner, the ceremony and a farewell brunch, Zola recommends listing them together on an itinerary when every guest is invited to all of them. Send it all at once, with one RSVP date, and ask guests to reply for each event so you get a separate count for every meal.

How Digital Invitations Change the Timing

An online invitation removes printing, addressing and postage time. Your send date can be the date you planned, instead of two weeks earlier to allow for the mail. Late changes are easier too, because you can update the details instead of reprinting.

What does not change is your guests' side. They still need several weeks to check calendars, arrange childcare or book travel. So keep the same six to eight week window for a local wedding, and do not send much earlier just because you can. An invitation that arrives too early is easy to forget.

Reminders are where online invitations help most. You can send the same link again on WhatsApp, text or email in a minute. With Nimtto, guests reply right on the invitation, and you see who is coming, how many, and to which events in your dashboard, which makes it easy to spot who still needs a nudge. For tone and manners, see our online invitation etiquette guide.

A destination wedding invitation with a coastal design shown on a phone

RSVP Deadline and Reminder Cadence

Work backward from your caterer's final headcount date. Set the RSVP deadline a week or two before it, so you have time to chase late replies.

A simple reminder rhythm:

1. One week before the deadline: a friendly first reminder to anyone who has not replied. Greenvelope suggests this timing.
2. One or two days after the deadline: a final reminder, also Greenvelope's suggestion.
3. About two to three weeks before the wedding: phone anyone still missing. Emily Post recommends calling stragglers around this point.

Three touches is enough. More than that starts to feel like pressure.

What to Do If You Are Running Late

Being late is common and fixable. The goal is to give guests as much notice as you can and make replying easy.

- Tell close family and key guests first. A personal call or message the same day you set the date is worth more than any card.
- Skip the save the date if the wedding is less than four months away. Send the invitation instead.
- Shorten the reply window, not the notice. Keep at least two to three weeks for replies if you can.
- Choose a format that sends fast. An online invitation goes out the day it is ready. Nimtto's design help usually takes one to three business days.

Emily Post also notes that if you invite a second group of guests later, they should still get at least four weeks to reply.

If your wedding is in X weeks

- 16 weeks or more: you are on time. Send a save the date now if guests travel, invitations at 6 to 8 weeks.
- 12 weeks: skip save the dates for local guests. Send invitations to far-away guests now, everyone else in a month.
- 8 weeks: send all invitations this week, RSVP due in four weeks.
- 6 weeks: send today, RSVP due in three weeks, and call family personally.
- 4 weeks or less: call or message everyone, send the invitation the same day, and ask for replies within one to two weeks.

Wording to Copy for Every Step

Save the date message:
Save the date!
Emma and James are getting married on Saturday, June 12, 2027, in Portland, Oregon.
Invitation and details to follow. We hope you can make it!

Invitation message:
Hi [Guest's name]!
Our wedding is on Saturday, June 12, 2027, and we'd love for you to celebrate with us.
Here's the invitation with times, venues and maps: [link]
Please reply on the invitation by May 15.
Love, Emma and James

RSVP reminder 1:
Hi [Guest's name], just a friendly reminder to reply to our wedding invitation by May 15.
It only takes a minute: [link]
We hope to see you there!

Final RSVP reminder:
Hi [Guest's name], we're giving our final numbers to the venue this week.
Could you let us know if you can make it by Friday? Here's the link again: [link]
Thank you so much!

Update message:
Hi [Guest's name], a quick update for our wedding on June 12:
the ceremony now starts at 5:00 p.m. instead of 4:30 p.m.
Everything else stays the same. Full details: [link]

"We missed your reply" note:
Hi [Guest's name], we haven't seen your reply yet and didn't want you to miss out!
Will you be able to join us on June 12? A quick yes or no is perfect.
Here's the invitation: [link]

Need help with the main invitation text? Our wedding invitation wording examples cover formal, casual and special situations.

Put your RSVP date in your own calendar with two reminders: one week before and one day after. You will not have to remember the cadence yourself.

Final Thoughts

Timing is about your guests' plans, not the stationery. Give people enough notice to arrange their lives, a clear date to reply by, and a gentle nudge or two. Do that and your count will be ready when your caterer asks.

### Is 3 months too early to send wedding invitations?
For a local wedding, three months is earlier than most guides suggest, and some guests may put the invitation aside and forget it. For a destination wedding or one with many guests flying in, three months or more is sensible.

### Do you have to send save the dates?
No, they are optional. They help most when guests need to travel, book time off or plan around a holiday weekend. For a small local wedding, an early invitation can do the same job.

### Does everyone who gets a save the date have to get an invitation?
Yes. A save the date is a promise that an invitation will follow, so only send one to people you are sure you will invite.

### Should online wedding invitations be sent earlier or later than paper ones?
Around the same time. You skip printing and mailing, so you can send closer to the usual date, but guests still need the same weeks to plan and reply.

### What if guests have not replied by the RSVP deadline?
Send one friendly message a day or two after the deadline, then call anyone still missing. Most late replies come from people who simply forgot.

### Can I send wedding invitations at different times to different guests?
Yes, as long as everyone gets enough time to reply. Guests traveling far can get theirs earlier; just keep the RSVP date the same for everyone so your count is ready on time.

### How do I collect RSVPs for several wedding events?
Ask guests to reply per event so you get a separate count for each one. Our guide on [collecting RSVPs online](/international/blog/how-to-collect-rsvps-online/) walks through the setup.
